title: Strict input refuses an undeclared field, a second document, an anchor, a merge key and a duplicate key
given: One service declaration with a correct head.
when: The text adds an unknown field, a second document, an anchor, a merge key, a non-string key or a duplicate collection key.
then: The parser refuses the declaration and names the file and the line.

title: Strict input holds the size limit and the nesting limit
given: A declaration larger than 4 MiB, and a declaration with 130 nesting levels.
when: The parser reads each one.
then: The parser refuses both and reports the byte limit and the nesting limit.

title: An archetype that the registry does not hold is refused
given: A project with a loaded registry.
when: The declaration names an archetype that the registry does not hold.
then: Checking reports an archetype fault that names the archetype.

title: Two entities with one name are refused
given: A valid project.
when: The declaration declares the entity Widget two times.
then: Checking reports that the entity is defined more than one time.

title: Two fields with one name in one entity are refused
given: A valid project.
when: One entity declares the field label two times.
then: Checking reports a duplicate field name.

title: A constraint that does not suit the field type is refused
given: A valid project.
when: A field puts a string constraint on a number, or a number constraint on a string, or enum values on another type.
then: Checking reports one fault for each constraint that does not suit the type.

title: Two collections with one name are refused
given: A valid project.
when: The declaration holds two collections with the same name.
then: Checking reports a duplicate collection name.

title: A collection that names an entity the declaration does not declare is refused
given: A valid project.
when: A collection names an entity that the declaration does not declare.
then: Checking reports that the entity is not defined.

title: A slot binding to a slot that no component declares is refused
given: A project whose components declare a known set of slots.
when: A slot binding names a slot outside that set.
then: Checking refuses the binding and names the available slots.

title: A slot binding to a collection the declaration does not declare is refused
given: A valid project with one collection.
when: A slot binding names another collection.
then: Checking refuses the binding and names the available collections.

title: A slot binding with no operator is refused
given: A valid project with one slot.
when: The slot binding holds no gate, chain or fan-out.
then: Checking refuses the binding and names the three operators.

title: A slot binding with more than one operator is refused
given: A valid project with one slot.
when: The slot binding holds a gate, a chain and a fan-out together.
then: Checking refuses the binding and requires one operator.

title: A binding to a slot that no generator invokes is refused
given: A component declares the slot resolve_field, and no generator in the build consumes it.
when: The declaration binds a fill to that slot.
then: Checking reports that no resolved generator consumes the slot.

title: One refusal reports every semantic fault together
given: A declaration with four separate faults.
when: Checking runs one time.
then: The result holds a fault for each one of the four, and not the first fault alone.

title: An unknown setting, a wrong value type and an inactive component are refused
given: A component that declares one string setting.
when: The declaration misspells the setting, gives it a number, names a component that is not active, or gives a value in place of a map.
then: Checking refuses each one, and generation refuses it with the same config fault.

title: A setting value must suit its declared type and its value set
given: A setting schema for each supported type, with lists and nested objects.
when: A value of the wrong type, a value outside the value set, a null value or an unknown nested key is checked.
then: The check reports a fault and names the path and the expected type.

title: Scaffolding refuses an existing path and changes no existing file
given: A project that already holds service.yaml, the registry config, the .stego directory or the fills directory, as a file, a directory or a link.
when: Scaffolding runs.
then: Scaffolding fails. The existing file keeps its content, and no file outside the project changes.

title: Generation uses the result of the one checking stage
given: A declaration with a semantic fault.
when: The validate command runs, then the plan runs.
then: The plan fails with the same fault text that checking reports. No generator runs.

title: Checking writes no file when it refuses a declaration
given: A project with a faulty declaration, an existing output file and an existing state record.
when: The validate, plan and apply commands each run.
then: Each command fails. The output file and the state record keep their content, and no go.mod appears.

title: Recovery completes an interrupted apply, so output and record always agree
given: A project with applied output and a new plan.
when: Apply fails at each journal point in turn, and recover runs.
then: Plan and drift refuse until recovery runs. After recovery the output matches the state record and no drift remains.

title: Drift detection fails when a generated file no longer matches its recorded hash
given: A project with applied output and recorded file hashes.
when: A generated file is edited by hand and drift detection runs.
then: The result names the modified file and reports drift.

title: A state record whose input manifest disagrees with it is refused
given: An applied state record with an input manifest.
when: The service hash or the registry reference in the manifest differs from the applied value.
then: State validation refuses the record.

title: Apply refuses a plan whose registry digest differs from the live registry
given: A plan from a loaded registry.
when: The registry content digest in the plan state is replaced and apply runs.
then: Apply fails with a registry error and writes no output.

title: A changed component generator shows as an update in the next plan
given: A project applied from one component generator output.
when: The component produces new content and plan runs again.
then: The plan marks the generated file as an update.

title: A registry change that does not affect output leaves every generated file unchanged
given: A project with applied output and a recorded registry digest.
when: A comment is added to a component declaration and apply runs.
then: The state record gains the new registry digest. Every generated file stays unchanged.

title: A new generation run restores the generated output without a hand edit
given: A project with applied output.
when: A generated file is edited by hand, then plan and apply run.
then: The plan names the file as an update. Apply restores the generated content and leaves no drift.

title: Qualification fails when the release tag does not point at the source commit
given: A qualified source commit and a published release tag.
when: The tag points at another commit and release verification runs.
then: Qualification fails.

title: Qualification fails when a required CI job has no success conclusion
given: A complete set of CI runs at the source commit.
when: One required checks job is absent from the job list.
then: Qualification fails.

title: Release verification cross-checks every published asset digest and the evidence notes
given: A published immutable release at the qualified commit.
when: Qualification runs with --verify-release.
then: It installs the release through the consumer path. It reports the asset digests and confirms that the notes hold the run and the compiler digest.

title: Installation refuses a platform other than Linux amd64 before any download
given: An installation request for a published release.
when: The machine reports aarch64, or the revision is not a full commit, or the result directory exists.
then: Installation fails and makes no API call.

title: Installation verifies both signatures before it puts the binary in place
given: A published release with four assets.
when: Installation downloads and verifies the assets.
then: The compiler and the build record are both authenticated while the result directory does not yet exist. The published bytes then match the downloaded bytes.

title: The version command reports the current build record
given: A built stego binary.
when: The version command runs with --json.
then: The record in the output equals the current build identity.

title: Apply writes the current build identity into the service state record
given: A project ready for apply.
when: Apply runs, and then a changed build record is offered in the plan.
then: The state record holds the current build identity. Apply refuses a substituted record and leaves the state unchanged.

title: The emitted store refuses weak transport and keeps the loopback exception narrow
when: Builds a database configuration for each sslmode, and for each host under both values of the test exception setting.
then: Expects every weak mode refused, plaintext allowed only to a literal loopback address while the setting is 1, and a safe error for any other value of the setting.

title: The emitted store checks the chain, the server name and the TLS version on a real connection
when: Opens a real TLS connection with a valid certificate, then with a wrong server name, then with a wrong trust root.
then: Expects the valid certificate accepted and both failures refused.

title: The emitted queue commits the message with the application write
when: Writes an application row and enqueues one message in one transaction, then rolls back, and then repeats the same work and commits.
then: Expects no visible data before the end of the transaction, no row and no message after the rollback, and both after the commit.

title: The emitted queue refuses an invalid payload before it uses the database
when: Validates ten invalid payloads, one valid payload, an enqueue with no transaction and a queue with no database.
then: Expects every invalid payload refused, the valid payload accepted, and an error for the missing transaction and the missing database.

title: A retry holds its own key and keeps the message identity
when: Claims two messages for one resource key and one for another key, retries the oldest message, and claims again.
then: Expects no claim for the successor during the delay, the same ID and a second attempt after it, and progress for the other key.

title: An expired lease cannot acknowledge or retry a message
when: Claims one message with a short lease, waits for the lease to expire, then acknowledges and retries with the old receipt.
then: Expects both calls to report no effect and the message to stay in the queue.

title: The emitted worker stores no handler error text
when: Runs the worker with a handler that returns an error which holds a private value.
then: Expects the stored failure code 'delivery-failed' and no part of the handler's error text.

title: A result after the attempt deadline is not acknowledged
when: Runs the worker with a handler that waits for its context to end and then returns success.
then: Expects no delivery count, a retry, and the stored failure code 'delivery-timeout'.

title: A claim with a lost client result returns no delivery
when: Runs the claim through a bounded SQL driver that returns a query error, and then a row error after one row.
then: Expects no delivery in both cases and the underlying error for the caller.

title: Recovery after an unknown claim result keeps the delivery contract
when: Loses the claim result, waits for normal lease expiry, and claims the message again.
then: Expects the same message IDs and contents, a higher attempt count, a new receipt token, and no effect from the old token.

title: The emitted stream header helper checks its requirements before it reads the stream
when: Passes empty, upper-case, spaced, over-long, duplicated, non-ASCII and too many header requirements, and a nil stream.
then: Expects the contract error with no header read and no message read.

title: The emitted timestamp conversion is checked and keeps presence and ownership
when: Converts the first, last, epoch, pre-epoch and zoned instants, then instants outside the range, then a nil and a present zero optional value, then a monotonic value.
then: Expects every supported instant preserved through the protobuf and JSON codecs, every out-of-range instant refused with no output and a fixed error, absence and present zero kept, each result owned, and the monotonic clock and local zone dropped.

title: The emitted response mapping keeps the wire contract and owns its output
when: Maps a stored model with present empty, optional, numeric, timestamp and JSON list values, then mutates the source, then supplies invalid values and bound violations.
then: Expects the declared wire contract and field presence kept, the result owned, and no partial message for an invalid value.

title: The emitted process supervisor bounds startup and cleanup and survives a failing callback
when: Runs the emitted supervisor for a clean return, a panic, a goroutine exit, a startup that never becomes ready, a cleanup that never finishes and a cancellation.
then: Expects the right exit result for each case within its bound, and the work goroutine joined afterwards.

title: The emitted health monitor and probe follow the process state and their bounds
when: Reads the probe paths before and after registration and during shutdown, checks the monitor address rule, runs the probe command with valid and invalid arguments, and runs it against a long body, a redirect, a wrong status and a stalled server, then takes the monitor port.
then: Expects liveness during initialization, readiness only after registration, both failing at shutdown, only a loopback address with a canonical port accepted, no metrics path, no domain work during a probe, each bad answer refused within its bound, and the process failing without opening the application when the monitor cannot bind.

title: The emitted process executable starts, serves and stops without a database
when: Builds and runs the emitted process executable for a normal run, a restart, and failures in Open, registration and cleanup, including a panic and a goroutine exit, with a TLS collector and signed tokens but no database.
then: Expects verified RPC calls, correlated startup and cleanup signals, no token or private error text in those signals, a fixed failure event with a non-zero exit, and bounded shutdown.

title: The emitted SDK client keeps verified TLS, its status, its bounds and its private errors
when: Builds the generated SDK with and without telemetry, then runs it against a TLS 1.3 service for a typed read, a 404 answer, a redirect, an over-large body, a malformed body, an escaping path, a short caller deadline, a plaintext base URL, an untrusted certificate, a path prefix and a closed client.
then: Expects the typed value and the status kept, each unsafe case refused with no bearer token in the error, the caller deadline honoured, plaintext and untrusted certificates refused, the close wait bounded, and a closed client refusing further calls.

title: The emitted SDK keeps the three nullable states in both directions
when: Sends an omitted member, an explicit null and a zero value for each nullable property through a real HTTPS exchange, then sets each state through the model methods.
then: Expects the member presence and the exact JSON value kept on the wire and in the decoded response, and each explicit state readable.

title: The emitted browser client keeps its origin, its CSRF exchange, its checks, its bounds and its private errors
when: Runs the emitted module in Node against a replaced fetch for a valid read and write, invalid input, invalid and unsafe responses, HTTP errors and exceptions, over-large and wrong-typed responses, cancellation and the concurrency limit, an unauthenticated session, a plaintext origin, a prototype-named operation, the whole-operation deadline, declared and undeclared API error codes, login, and valid and invalid trace contexts.
then: Expects same-origin uncached unredirected fetches with no credential header, a fresh CSRF token for each mutation, no request for invalid input, every unsafe response refused, errors that hold only fixed codes and a declared API code, each bound held with capacity released, no prototype change, and a trace context confined to one operation.

title: The emitted declarations compile under strict TypeScript and separate the two model directions
when: Compiles a caller module against the emitted declarations with the pinned strict TypeScript compiler.
then: Expects the valid calls to compile and expects a type error for an absent required argument, a wrong body member type, a response-only member in a request body and an OAuth credential in the request options.

title: A lost notice session stops the source and its subscriptions
when: Terminates the dedicated PostgreSQL backend of the source, then reads the subscription, subscribes again, and starts a replacement source.
then: Expects the supervised task and the subscription to fail with ErrEventSourceUnavailable, the failed source to refuse a new subscription, and the replacement source to deliver the next notice.

title: The emitted backend keeps strict cookies, hides tokens and proxies with server credentials
when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers, restarts the backend, then signs out.
then: Expects the login cookie Lax and the active cookie Strict, both Secure, HttpOnly and host-only, no token in the session response, only the server access token and four permitted headers at the API, and no upstream Set-Cookie.

title: The emitted backend refuses requests without an exact origin, a CSRF token, or with browser credentials
when: Sends thirteen requests with a missing, wrong, repeated or same-site origin, a missing or repeated CSRF header, a browser bearer token, a duplicate cookie, a bad method and an oversize body.
then: Expects the stated status for each case, and expects that no denied request reached the API.

title: The emitted store encrypts session records and binds them to the cookie hash
when: Creates a session with an access and a refresh token, then reads the stored row and opens the record with another cookie ID and with one changed byte.
then: Expects a 32-byte hash, no plaintext token and no raw cookie ID in the row, and refusal of both the foreign cookie ID and the changed ciphertext.

title: Two emitted backend instances share one token renewal
when: Expires the access token, holds the provider refresh request, then asks for the session from both backend instances.
then: Expects the second instance to wait, both requests to succeed, the new access token at the API, and exactly one refresh request.

title: A completed renewal cannot restore a session that sign-out removed
when: Starts a renewal on one instance, holds the provider request, then signs out on the second instance and releases the renewal.
then: Expects the sign-out to succeed, the later API request to return 401, and both the old and the rotated token to be revoked.

title: A lost or stale renewal requires a new login and is not retried
when: Drops the provider refresh response, and separately ages an existing refresh claim past its deadline, then sends two API requests.
then: Expects 401 for both requests and expects no second refresh request.

title: A waiter for an active renewal has a deadline and keeps its cookie
when: Claims a renewal, then asks for the session, then asks again with a cancelled context.
then: Expects 503 with Retry-After inside three seconds, a retained session cookie, a cancelled waiter that stops inside one second, and no use of the refresh token.

title: The emitted asset routes keep a narrow script policy and refuse unsafe paths
when: Requests each declared route and asset, three undeclared paths, five unsafe return paths, and a plaintext or wrong-host address.
then: Expects a policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, the script hashes only on index.html, 404 for each undeclared path, / for each unsafe return path, and 400 for the wrong host.

title: The emitted backend refuses an identity host that shares the console cookie host
when: Starts the backend with an issuer on the console host and another port, then with a discovered authorization endpoint on the console host.
then: Expects the backend to refuse to start in both cases.

title: Unrelated PostgreSQL environment values change no identity, no transport and no session
when: Sets 18 PostgreSQL environment values, builds the configuration from explicit Options, and then sets PGSERVICE.
then: Expects the explicit identity, verified TLS with the Options host name, no fallback, the four read-only session parameters, and a refusal for PGSERVICE.

title: The sign-out confirmation page does not sign out and keeps its same-origin referrer policy
when: Opens the confirmation page, then posts the form with a missing, null, foreign or repeated Origin value and with four invalid bodies.
then: Expects the page to keep the session and revoke nothing, Referrer-Policy same-origin on that page and no-referrer elsewhere, 403 or 400 for each invalid form, and sign-out only after a valid form.

title: The emitted provider sign-out request is minimal and refuses unsafe endpoints
when: Builds the provider sign-out target for six unsafe discovered endpoints and for one valid HTTPS endpoint.
then: Expects a refusal for each unsafe endpoint, and expects exactly two query parameters, client_id and post_logout_redirect_uri, for the valid one.

title: The emitted key reader accepts only a small ring of distinct canonical keys
when: Reads four valid key files, then twenty-six invalid files with bad size, bad base64, a duplicate key, four keys, unknown or repeated JSON fields and trailing data.
then: Expects the valid files to keep their key order, and expects every invalid file to return the fixed error with a nil key ring.

title: The emitted runtime uses the fixed authenticated transport and the generated identity
when: Starts the emitted runtime on an HTTPS page, records one span, one log and one metric, then flushes.
then: Expects one POST to each of the three same-origin signal paths, same-origin credentials with a refused redirect, the session token in the header only, the generated service name in every body, and no reported failure.

title: Export failures stay inside the public categories and the response limit
when: Answers an export with a private error body, then with a partial-success record, then with a response above 16 KiB.
then: Expects a failed flush each time, an export_failed report for traces, and no private or secret text in the reported failures.

title: The emitted runtime refuses an insecure page and an invalid trace ID
when: Supplies invalid options and invalid root trace IDs, then moves the page to http.
then: Expects every invalid option and trace ID refused, a valid span ID shape, no fetch call, and a refusal to start on the http page.

title: The emitted CLI keeps its transport, file and input boundaries through a real TLS workflow
when: Logs in with a token file against a TLS server, runs create, read, list and delete commands, rotates the token, then supplies a public configuration, a writable configuration directory, a public token file, a configuration symlink, a FIFO, invalid arguments, invalid body files, a redirect answer, a private error answer and a duplicate-key answer, and finally an http destination.
then: Expects mode 0600 configuration without the token, the rotated token read by the next command, exact response numbers, each unsafe or invalid case refused, one request for each rejected answer, no private text or token in an error, and the external token file retained after logout.

title: The emitted CLI holds the declared empty response contract
when: Declares success codes 202, 204 and 205 with and without an explicit empty code, answers with an empty body, a JSON body, an invalid body and an unaccepted code, then declares a repeated, unaccepted or oversized empty code list.
then: Expects an empty body accepted only for a declared empty code and for 204 and 205, valid JSON required for every other accepted code, no output for a failed command, and each invalid declaration refused before the server is called.

title: The emitted CLI reserves a private output file before the request
when: Runs a sensitive scoped command with no output option, then with an existing file, a symlink, a FIFO, a directory, a writable parent and a missing parent, then with a new file, a repeated file, a failed API answer and an explicit stdout selection.
then: Expects the empty private reservation present during the request, every unsafe destination refused with no stdout output, the secret written only to the new private file, an existing file never replaced, the empty reservation removed after a failure, and only the name field in the request body.

title: The emitted CLI reports only API identity and protects token export
when: Runs the identity command against a TLS API, then requests raw and decoded token output with and without an output file, with both options together, and against a failed, incomplete and duplicate-key answer.
then: Expects the report built from the API answer only, the token and the private and local claims absent from the default output, token export refused without an output file and without an API call, mode 0600 export files with exact decoded numbers, and no output file after a failure.

title: An invalid identity or certificate input is refused
when: Builds the configuration for four valid hosts, and then for nine invalid identities and certificate inputs.
then: Expects every valid host accepted, and every socket path, malformed host, empty field, private key and trailing data refused.

title: The emitted CLI verifies the OIDC browser login
when: Runs browser login against a TLS provider that returns a wrong issuer, a plaintext token endpoint, a wrong nonce, a wrong audience, an expired token, a wrong authorized party, a wrong token hash and a changed issuer claim, and answers the callback with a wrong state and then twice with the correct state.
then: Expects the correct case to return the subject and the rotated refresh token, every invalid issuer, endpoint and claim refused, the openid scope and the S256 challenge in the authorization URL, a loopback callback, HTTP 400 for the wrong state, HTTP 409 for the second callback, and no token in the command output.

title: The emitted CLI refreshes once across processes and removes the session at logout
when: Saves an expired OIDC session, starts four child processes that each request credentials, then runs logout.
then: Expects one provider refresh for the four processes, the rotated session saved without a pending mark, one revocation request, and the local configuration removed.

title: The emitted apply command stops before writes and reports partial results
when: Applies three documents against a TLS API that denies the second lookup, returns a malformed list, refuses the second write or answers the second write with a server error, then applies two documents where the second omits a late required create field.
then: Expects no write at all for a lookup or list failure, the statuses created, failed or unknown and not_attempted for a write failure, no private response text in the output or the error, and no write for the missing required field.

title: An owned resource converges, keeps its preconditions, and reports absence only after it is gone.
when: The generated client calls Ensure twice with the same desired Widget, then changes it, then calls DeleteOwned twice against a fake API server.
then: The second Ensure sends no write, the patch and the delete carry the observed UID and resource version, the first DeleteOwned reports false while the deletion is pending, the second reports true, and the caller's desired object is unchanged.

title: Every write carries strict field validation, keeps the caller's options, and reports only status metadata.
when: The generated client sends a POST, a PUT and a PATCH with a caller query that already selects weaker validation, then sends two writes with a malformed query.
then: Each request has exactly one Strict field-validation value and keeps the caller's dryRun option, the rejected write returns only the method and the status, the malformed queries make no request, and the server receives exactly three writes.

title: Observation lists a bounded snapshot, keeps its cursor across reconnects, and lists again after expired history.
when: A fake API server returns a two-page list, one watch event, a bookmark, an expired-history error, and a later list and delete, while the token file changes during observation.
then: The callback receives RESET, REPLACE, MODIFIED, RESET, REPLACE and DELETED in that order, each list page is bounded and keeps its cursor, the watch uses the snapshot version without paging options, and the reconnect uses the replaced token.

title: Deployment availability requires a complete current rollout and fails closed on a malformed observation.
when: The availability check reads an available Deployment and then thirteen pending variants and twelve invalid variants, including exact int64 generations.
then: The available Deployment passes, each pending variant reports false without an error, each foreign or malformed variant returns ErrResourceObservation, and an out-of-range replica requirement is refused.

title: Route exposure needs admission, a successful probe, and an unchanged observation.
when: The Route helper runs against a fake API server in eleven modes, including a pending admission, a failed probe, a replaced UID, a changed resource version, a removed Route, a foreign namespace in the response, and an invalid target.
then: Only the ready mode returns true, the probe runs once and only after admission passes, a pending or changed observation returns false without an error, and an invalid target or a canceled context reaches no API call.

title: Server TLS Secret verification uses explicit trust, refuses mixed PEM data, and hides its reasons.
when: The verifier reads a valid owned TLS Secret, then variants with a self-supplied CA, a private key or extra text in the certificate field, a second private key, oversized data, a long chain, an expired certificate, and a certificate for the other purpose.
then: The valid Secret returns only its certificate bytes even with an untrusted ca.crt field, and every invalid variant returns ErrResourceObservation with no extra text and no returned data.

title: Registry credentials are created, rotated from a private file, and refused when identity or the file mode is wrong.
when: The credential operation runs in 25 modes against a fake API server, then reconciles from a private file, rotates that file, and finally makes the file readable by other users.
then: The namespace owner and UID are checked before and after each write, a replaced namespace or a foreign Secret permits no write, a conflict is not retried, repeated data writes nothing, rotation writes exactly once, the public file is refused, and no error contains credential data.

title: An invalid read opens no connection
when: Checks five invalid dial routes, three valid routes, and five reads with an invalid context, query, argument or destination.
then: Expects each invalid input refused, and expects that no returned error is a remote *Error.

title: The rendered service, worker and RPC manifests keep the restricted Pod, the HTTPS probes and the narrow external egress rules
when: The generator writes a project with a worker and an RPC process, and the generated renderer runs for each workload with valid and invalid arguments.
then: The service Pod mounts no token, runs as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, and all three probes use HTTPS. The worker uses one replica and Recreate, has no container port and no ingress rule. The RPC Service exposes only port 9090. Each external endpoint rule holds one host prefix and one TCP port. An invalid image, namespace, group, workload or endpoint binding returns an error and no output.

title: The browser Pod keeps the local application container inside a separate boundary
when: A browser service declares one local application, and the test renders the generated manifest template.
then: The Pod mounts no token and uses no host namespace. Both containers refuse privilege escalation, use a read-only root filesystem and drop all capabilities. The application container has no port, its own Secret and temporary volumes, and a fixed loopback listener. The Service exposes only port 8443, and a peer for the application port is refused.

title: The generated renderer splits scopes, sets the configuration digest, adds pull Secrets and keeps generated labels
when: The generator writes a project with allocation, RPC and Kubernetes access, and the generated scope, library and configuration checks run against the renderer.
then: The cluster and namespace manifests together hold the same objects as the full manifest, each with its own scope. An unknown kind or a wrong namespace stops the render. A supplied digest changes only the Pod template annotation, and an invalid digest returns no output. Pull Secrets appear as name references. An owner label that conflicts with a generated label is refused.

title: The Pod admission policy fails closed and holds the account, token and status rules
when: A profile adds a Pod runtime class and a declared Pod ServiceAccount, and the test compares the generated objects with the earlier set.
then: The new policy fails closed, its binding denies, and it selects only the installation marker and the profile. Its rules cover pods, pods/status and pods/ephemeralcontainers on CREATE and UPDATE. Its validations name the sealed account annotation, the automatic token field, the runtime class and the owner label. The existing policies and the worker configuration do not change.

title: The isolated allocation manifest fails closed and gives the allocator no policy or runtime write
when: An isolated profile declares an account, network isolation, a runtime class, Pod annotations and a capability grant, and the test reads every generated object.
then: All eight policies fail closed. No generated ClusterRole names validatingadmissionpolicies or runtimeclasses. The worker receives the security mode but no capability grant.

title: Network isolation gives narrow policy permissions and a deny-all policy shape
when: One profile selects network isolation and a second profile does not, and the test reads the generated roles and policies.
then: The allocator receives get and patch on the name stego-allocation plus create and list, and no update or delete. The admission guard requires the reserved name, an empty Pod selector, both policy types and no allow rule. It selects only the isolated profile. A profile without isolation receives no network permission.

title: The control account installer role carries one capability and no binding
when: The test reads every generated object for a plain declaration and for a declaration with related profiles.
then: The control account guard selects the control namespace on create and fails closed. Its expression reserves the fixed control account names and the generateName prefixes, and requires the installer capability. The installer ClusterRole holds one non-resource rule with the verb get. No ClusterRoleBinding selects that role, and no other generated object carries the capability.

title: An application Pod rule adds one denial and changes nothing else
when: An isolated profile adds one CEL Pod rule, and the test compares the generated policy with the policy built without that rule.
then: The rule is the last validation and keeps its exact expression and message. After the test removes it, the policy and the binding are equal to the earlier objects. The allocator runtime configuration holds no expression code. A repeated rule is refused.

title: The built Deployment and Service keep the restricted profile, the read-only mounts and the private dependency contents
when: The generated library builds one Deployment and one Service from a complete widget declaration.
then: The Pod mounts no token, uses the expected non-root security context with the RuntimeDefault profile, and each container uses the expected restricted security context. All three probes keep their deadlines and no host. The Secret volume uses mode 0440, the Secret and ConfigMap mounts are read-only, and the temporary mount is writable. The Service is a ClusterIP Service that targets the declared container port. The serialized output holds no dependency value and no host, privileged, subPath or exec field.

title: Changed dependency contents change only the configuration annotation
when: The declaration keeps every other field and rotates one Secret value, then changes one ConfigMap value.
then: The Pod template annotation stego.dev/config-sha256 changes each time. The rest of the Pod template is equal to the earlier template. The serialized output holds no rotated Secret value.

title: A verified read holds the session, the deadline and the error contract
when: Reads through a TLS fixture in front of a real PostgreSQL service, with a bound value, a write statement, an oversized result, no rows, a short deadline, a wrong password, a wrong host name and a wrong trust root.
then: Expects the bound value unchanged, the write refused with SQLSTATE 25006 and no table created, the deadline honored, a safe authentication error with no password text, both TLS faults refused, and recovery after the failed reads.

title: Unsafe or ambiguous declarations return no resources
when: Each case changes one field of the widget declaration to an unsafe or ambiguous value and calls Build.
then: Build returns the fixed declaration error and no resources for a missing, extra or wrong-kind dependency, a missing environment key, a tagged or malformed image, the default account, a zero file group, an excess or zero resource amount, a probe with a wrong port, a host, a query, an encoded path or a zero deadline, an unsafe or overlapping mount path, an unused or oversize volume, and a service port with no target.

title: A repeated message ID stops the application write
when: Enqueues one message, then writes an application row and enqueues the same message ID in one transaction.
then: Expects the enqueue to fail, the commit to fail, no application row, and one stored message.

title: Notices reach every session after the commit, in commit order
when: Subscribes two separate sessions, enqueues inside an open transaction, commits, and then enqueues two messages for one resource key in one transaction.
then: Expects no notice before the commit, the notice in both sessions after it, and the two notices in commit order.

title: Concurrent enqueues serialize before the sequence
when: Enqueues for one resource key in one open transaction, then enqueues the same key in a second transaction, and commits the first.
then: Expects the second enqueue to wait for the predecessor, and expects the first message in the next claim.

title: Concurrent workers claim distinct messages
when: Runs eight workers that each claim eight of 32 queued messages.
then: Expects no error, 32 claimed messages, and no message in two batches.

title: A changed lease token cannot acknowledge a message
when: Replaces the lease token in the database while the handler runs.
then: Expects one lost lease, no delivery, and the retained message.

title: An unknown destination stays in the queue
when: Enqueues a message for a destination that the worker has no handler for.
then: Expects the stored code 'destination-unknown', no handler call, and the unknown-destination counter above zero.

title: Unsafe worker limits are refused and the retry delay stays bounded
when: Builds the worker with seven unsafe configurations and with a nil handler, then samples the retry delay for four attempt counts.
then: Expects an error for each unsafe input, and every delay inside the configured bounds.

title: The worker holds its concurrency limit and copies its handlers
when: Queues eight messages, removes the handler from the caller's map after construction, and starts a second run.
then: Expects at most two active handlers, all eight deliveries, no active handler at the end, and an error from the second run.

title: A database failure drops no message
when: Closes the connection pool while the worker runs.
then: Expects the database-failure counter above zero and no delivery.

title: The emitted database lifecycle keeps isolation, separate roles, recorded objects and one operation for each resource
when: Runs the whole lifecycle on a dedicated PostgreSQL server: creation, repeat calls, repair, failed activation, isolation drift, quarantine, a replaced role OID, an unrecorded role, concurrent calls, and deletion.
then: Expects a login that reaches only its own database, an owner that cannot log in, a login with no administrative rights, a refusal for a changed or unrecorded object, ErrDatabaseBusy for a concurrent operation, and retained application data.

title: The blocked view holds one entry for each stuck key
when: Claims two of four messages, reads the blocked view, retries one key with a failure code, makes that key ready, and reads the view again with two invalid limits.
then: Expects one entry for each in-flight key with its destination and timing, the failure code retained, the ready key absent, and both invalid limits refused.

title: Dead letters and purge keep the unexhausted messages
when: Exhausts one resource key with three claims and retries, lists the dead letters, purges them, and gives an invalid limit.
then: Expects only the exhausted messages listed and removed, the fresh message retained, and the invalid limit refused.

title: A process crash commits nothing and releases its lease
when: Runs a helper subprocess that exits abruptly with an open transaction, and again with an active claim.
then: Expects no application row and no message after the first exit, and recovery of the same message with a higher attempt count after the lease expires.

title: The event source holds its subscription and queue bounds
when: Overruns the buffer of a slow subscription, fills the subscription limit, cancels one subscription, and closes the source.
then: Expects ErrSlowConsumer for the slow reader, ErrEventCapacity at the limit, the cancellation returned, and ErrEventSourceUnavailable after the close.

title: Shutdown acknowledges a delivery that completed
when: Cancels the worker while its handler runs, and lets the handler return success after the cancellation.
then: Expects the worker to wait for the handler, one delivery, and an empty queue.

title: A retry keeps the message identity and stores no error text
when: Fails the first delivery of one message with an error that holds a private value, then lets both messages succeed.
then: Expects three handler calls in order, the same ID for both attempts, one retry, no lost lease, and an empty queue.

title: An attempt deadline retains the failed message
when: Runs a handler that waits for its context to end.
then: Expects the attempt to stop at its deadline and the message to stay in the queue for retry.

title: A canceled claim returns the cancellation
when: Claims with a context that is already canceled.
then: Expects context.Canceled from the claim.

title: A prepared credential stays out of formatting and JSON
when: Formats the credential in five formats as a value, a pointer, a struct field and a map value, marshals it to JSON, and prepares credentials with a nil context and an empty key.
then: Expects no server identity and no password in any output, a failed JSON export, and no credential from an invalid preparation.

title: SQL names come from the keys and refuse unsafe input
when: Derives names from a key whose resource holds a DROP DATABASE statement, repeats with another installation scope, and gives three invalid keys, a generated password and two invalid specifications.
then: Expects safe prefixed names, separate owner and login names, different names for the other scope, and a refusal for every invalid key, context and credential.

title: The emitted client uses no global telemetry provider
when: Installs global trace, metric and log providers, then calls the lifecycle operations with no telemetry runtime in the context.
then: Expects no exported span, no scope metric and no log output.

title: A schema operation checks its inputs before it runs schema code
when: Calls WithDatabaseOwner with a nil context, a nil callback, an unpinned server, an unmanaged database and an invalid credential.
then: Expects an error for each call, ErrDatabaseServer for the unpinned server, and no call to the schema callback.

title: A cycle keeps its failure across process replacement
when: Fails one action in the first cycle, then completes the cycle with a new call, and then runs two more cycles.
then: Expects the failure and ErrCycleFailed, the retained failure for the completed cycle, no provider error text in the checkpoint, and a new full cycle after it.

title: Run owns its telemetry and excludes private data
when: Runs the public entry point with a TLS collector, a private resource value and private callback errors, with sampling enabled and disabled.
then: Expects independent operation roots, provider spans under them, the bounded queue counts, complete flush, and no private value in any exported batch or local log.

title: An uncertain save requires a fresh load
when: Saves with a lost result, a wrong version and a mutated argument.
then: Expects no usable state and one write for each fault, and the saved value after a fresh load.

title: A slow scan finishes without an overlapping scan
when: Runs the controller with a scan that needs more time than the resync interval.
then: Expects no overlapping scan and the emitted item from the slow scan.

title: A transient action failure is recovered by the next scan
when: Fails the first action with an I/O error, then denies the second attempt.
then: Expects two attempts and the terminal error from the second one.

title: A canceled parent saves no checkpoint
when: Cancels the parent context inside the action of a checkpointed scan.
then: Expects context.Canceled and no save call.

title: An observation keeps its commit reserve
when: Runs an observation with a 300 ms parent deadline, a one-second work timeout and a 200 ms commit reserve, and returns success from the work callback after its deadline.
then: Expects the work deadline at the parent deadline less the reserve, a live commit context with the deadline error, a closed work context, and the deadline error from the call.

title: A sealed state record binds its key, its version and its bytes
when: Seals one record twice, opens it with four changed keys and another version, flips each bit in turn, and formats the protector and the value.
then: Expects no plaintext in the envelope, a new envelope for each seal, a correct round trip, a refusal for every changed key, version and damaged byte, redacted formats, and a failed JSON export.

title: The keyed queue starts paused and keeps its work
when: Adds one key before the baseline, then sets the baseline, then resets it and adds the key again.
then: Expects no take before the baseline and during the reset, and the retained key after each one.

title: Client signals exclude every private input
when: Exports spans, logs and metrics to a TLS collector for nine failed operations with private keys, passwords, queries and arguments.
then: Expects nine correlated spans and events under the private scope, the fixed outcomes, and no 'private-' value or password in any exported message.

title: An invalid key consumes no capacity
when: Adds an empty key, a 1,025-byte key and a key that is not valid UTF-8.
then: Expects ErrKey for each key and no queue entry.

title: A due retry runs before a newer key
when: Fails one key, makes its retry due, and adds a new key.
then: Expects the due retry before the new key.

title: Probe commands start no application work
when: Runs the live probe and the ready probe against a local server, then three invalid argument sets and five invalid monitor addresses.
then: Expects success for both probes with no application callback, and exit code 2 for every invalid argument and address.

title: A denied publication returns an error
when: Answers the produce request with TopicAuthorizationFailed for every partition.
then: Expects ErrUnavailable from Publish.

title: The runtime refuses a missing queue schema
when: Drops the outbox schema, then builds the runtime with an empty configuration.
then: Expects a construction error that names the schema, before any broker connection.

title: The runtime delivers a message that a former process left
when: Closes the first runtime, commits one message, starts a replacement runtime, and runs it twice.
then: Expects ErrClosed from the closed runtime, one delivery by the replacement, an error from the second run, and the record at the broker.

title: A closed publisher refuses a later publish
when: Publishes from 16 goroutines, closes the publisher twice, and publishes again.
then: Expects every goroutine to return, no fault from the repeated close, and ErrClosed from the last publish.

title: A committed message reaches TLS Kafka and leaves the queue
when: Enqueues one message with an application row in one transaction, waits, commits, and then consumes the record.
then: Expects no broker call before the commit, one delivery after it, an empty queue, the retained application row, the expanded JSONB payload, and the durable message ID in a header.

title: Concurrent reads share no state
when: Runs 80 reads of one group from eight goroutines.
then: Expects the same correct value from every read and no error.

title: Boundary values and an explicit empty value are accepted
when: Reads the group with the lowest and the highest permitted values, with an explicitly empty optional string, and checks the int64 boundaries.
then: Expects every boundary value accepted and kept unchanged.

title: The emitted runtime opens its watch before the first scan and runs serial actions
when: Runs the controller with a source whose scan emits one live record and one retained deletion record.
then: Expects the watch open before the scan, no parallel action, and both typed items in order.

title: The loader reads the process environment
when: Sets the five environment variables and calls the generated loader.
then: Expects the exact typed settings value.

title: Queue overflow cancels the session, joins its workers and rescans
when: Fills the bounded queue while one action is active, then lets the recovery session run.
then: Expects the active action canceled, every worker joined, a second watch session, and a new scan after it.

title: Invalid Unicode in a token payload never becomes an identity field
when: Signs a payload whose username claim holds an unpaired surrogate escape, in three shapes.
then: Expects every token refused and an empty username in the returned identity.

title: Stop on the emitted key source cancels a retrieval that is already running
when: Holds the key endpoint open inside a refresh that a verification started, then calls Stop twice.
then: Expects the pending verification to return an error inside two seconds, so shutdown cancelled the retrieval.

title: A zero key source denies every token
when: Verifies a token against a zero JWKSVerifier value, then calls Stop twice.
then: Expects the token refused and both Stop calls safe.

title: The emitted grant document reader refuses an ambiguous document
when: Parses a valid document, an empty array, and seventeen ambiguous documents that change the member names, the member types, the Unicode, the whitespace, the trailing data and the size.
then: Expects the valid document accepted, the empty array accepted and denying, and every ambiguous document refused with a nil policy.

title: The emitted grant policy holds its bounds and its uniqueness rule
when: Builds a policy from a repeated grant, from 1,025 grants, and from grants with an empty issuer, an empty subject, an oversize target, a spaced operation and a slashed resource.
then: Expects every construction refused.

title: An empty target and a literal asterisk target stay exact
when: Builds a policy for an empty target and then for a literal asterisk target, and asks each for its own target and for another target.
then: Expects the exact target permitted and the other target denied in both cases.

title: The emitted verifier serves concurrent callers
when: Verifies one valid token from sixteen workers, twenty times each.
then: Expects every call to return the same verified subject with no error.

title: The emitted SSO handler refuses an unusable startup context
when: Starts the handler with a nil context, then with a canceled context, then with a usable context.
then: Expects the nil and canceled contexts refused and the usable context accepted.

title: The emitted SSO startup uses the process runtime and keeps its records private
when: Starts the handler with a nil runtime, a nil context, a usable pair, an invalid key document, a canceled context and an expired deadline, uses the runtime after the handler stops, then reads the local signal output.
then: Expects the invalid pairs refused, the runtime still usable after the handler closes, the five fixed outcomes in order, and no key path, key document or issuer in the output.

title: A denied operation stops the runtime and is not hidden
when: Denies the watch, then the scan, then the action, in three separate runs.
then: Expects the denial from Run in each run, and exactly one watch attempt.

title: The emitted identity helpers compose names and ownership from the declared ids
when: Builds the identity for each declared kind, then builds two identities from an empty id.
then: Expects the composed client name, the ownership keys under the reserved prefix, the legacy form and its rename map, no legacy form for a kind that declares none, and ErrOwnership for an empty id.

title: The emitted binding helpers refuse a foreign or partly owned client
when: Binds a live client that holds the current ownership keys, then one that holds the complete legacy form, then five records with a nil client, a foreign name, mixed ownership, partial ownership and a wrong id.
then: Expects the current and complete legacy forms accepted, and ErrOwnership for every other record, including a client with no ownership key and a client with a foreign reserved key.

title: A legacy audience accepts a stored name only in its legacy form
when: Binds a legacy audience record by its stored public name, then binds a migrated record by that same stored name, then binds the migrated record by its generated name.
then: Expects the legacy form accepted, ErrOwnership for the migrated record under the stored name, and the generated name accepted.

title: The emitted client search stays inside its realm, fragment and page
when: Searches with a fragment that holds reserved URL characters, then with thirteen invalid fragments and four invalid pages.
then: Expects one request with the encoded fragment, the fixed search mode and the selected page, every invalid fragment and page refused, and no network request for an invalid argument.

title: A failed search from the emitted provider is not repeated or widened
when: Searches against a provider that denies the query, returns null, returns too many records and returns a repeated record.
then: Expects an error in each case, ErrResponse for the three invalid bodies, exactly one read, and no fall back to another query.

title: The emitted provider refuses an ambiguous provider response
when: Reads one client and then looks one up against eleven invalid response bodies.
then: Expects ErrResponse for a null body, an empty object, a different ID, a duplicate member, invalid Unicode, trailing data, a duplicate attribute, a repeated record, a foreign record and an empty ID.

title: An invalid administrator grant never reaches the provider API
when: Answers the token endpoint with five grants that have no token type, a wrong type, a zero lifetime, an oversize lifetime and a duplicate member.
then: Expects ErrResponse in each case and no API request.

title: The emitted provider validates identifiers and pages before any request
when: Looks up, pages and inspects clients, then reads seven unsafe identifiers and four invalid pages.
then: Expects every request inside the selected realm with the administrator credential, every unsafe identifier and invalid page refused, no network request for an invalid argument, and a cached administrator token.

title: A record with no explicit state is not treated as disabled
when: Disables a client whose record omits the enabled member and then whose record holds a null enabled member.
then: Expects ErrResponse in both cases and no write.

title: Credential rotation and an unauthorized answer clear the emitted provider's token cache
when: Reads a client, replaces the private credential file, reads again while the provider answers 401 with a private body, then reads once more.
then: Expects the rotated secret used for the next grant, the unauthorized read failed without the provider body and without a replay, and a new grant for the later read.

title: Invalid options open no source
when: Runs the controller with six option sets, each with one invalid capacity, policy, interval or timeout.
then: Expects an error for each set, and no call to the source.

title: Close and cancellation release every caller of the emitted provider
when: Holds the first authentication open, then calls with a canceled context, then with a short deadline, then closes the provider.
then: Expects the canceled caller released with context.Canceled, the waiting caller released with context.DeadlineExceeded, the first call canceled by Close, and ErrClosed for later work.

title: A span from the emitted provider keeps the caller trace and holds no request data
when: Reads a client through the provider inside a sampled caller span and inspects the provider request headers and the two recorded spans.
then: Expects the caller trace kept with a new span ID, no baggage or trace state sent, client spans with the response status, and no client name, provider ID, server URL or credential in the attributes.

title: The emitted probes hold their method policy and their construction bounds
when: Sends HEAD and POST to both probe paths, then builds a monitor with a nil context, a nil check, seventeen checks and a nil database.
then: Expects an empty body for HEAD, 405 with an Allow header for POST, and a refusal for every invalid construction.

title: A remote sampled flag cannot override the local zero ratio
when: Sets the sampling ratio to zero and sends a request that carries a sampled trace parent.
then: Expects the handler span not recording and no trace exported.

title: An invalid trace parent starts a root span
when: Sends four requests whose trace parent is absent, malformed, all zero and repeated.
then: Expects one exported root span for each request.

title: The emitted metric providers bound their series and balance their active counts
when: Starts one stream, then records three cycles of twice the series limit of distinct RPC methods, and flushes the meter after each cycle.
then: Expects the active counter at one for the open stream, no more than the series limit of histogram series, an overflow series that keeps every count, and the active counter back at zero.

title: Concurrent and replacement runtimes hold distinct identities
when: Creates and closes thirty-two runtimes at the same time with one service name.
then: Expects thirty-two valid and distinct UUID identities, and no change to an identity across its close.

title: Every signal and the local log share the runtime identity
when: Observes one request, logs one service event, closes the runtime, and reads the local output with the exported traces, logs and metrics.
then: Expects the same service name and instance identity in the local record and in all three exported signals, with two resource attributes only.

title: A handler panic invents no response and leaves no active request
when: Sends one request to a handler that panics with a private value, then reads the exported metrics and logs.
then: Expects the panic re-raised, no status attribute on the duration metric, error.type panic, the active counter at zero, an ERROR log record, and no private value in the export.

title: A blocked local log output stays bounded and does not block its caller
when: Holds the local writer inside one record, then logs three times the queue size of events, then closes the runtime.
then: Expects the caller never blocked, the drop count equal to the records beyond the bound, the shared shutdown budget held, and a refusal after the queue closes.

title: Watch setup has the operation deadline
when: Keeps the first watch setup open until its context ends, then denies the second setup.
then: Expects the setup to time out, a second attempt, the denial from Run, and no scan after a failed setup.

title: Outbound RPC signals keep the parent trace and isolate the caller metadata
when: Traces three outbound calls inside a caller span, with private authorization, trace parent, trace state and baggage metadata, for a sampled and an unsampled ratio.
then: Expects a child span of the caller trace, one injected trace parent with no trace state or baggage, the caller metadata unchanged, one completion for each call, the active counter at zero, and no private value in the export.

title: Database signals hold no statement data and map an unknown outcome
when: Traces six database calls with a private call name and the six outcome values, including a private outcome, for a sampled and an unsampled ratio.
then: Expects one completion for each call, the private outcome recorded as the fixed failure value, correlated client spans, idempotent completion, and no private value in the export.

title: The deployment export returns fixed file names and no private value
when: Exports a deployment environment from validated settings, replaces the token file and exports again, then exports for nine invalid cases.
then: Expects the fixed relative file names with the captured file contents, no token or source path in the environment, the replacement token in the later call with the earlier capture unchanged, every invalid case refused, and no private value in the error.

title: Outbound HTTPS signals keep the parent trace and send no private propagation
when: Traces five outbound HTTPS calls inside a caller span, with private authorization, trace parent, trace state and baggage headers, for a sampled and an unsampled ratio.
then: Expects a child span of the caller trace, one trace parent header with no trace state or baggage, the caller headers unchanged, one completion for each call, and no private value in the export.

title: Unsupported signal settings are refused and a blocked collector keeps one shutdown budget
when: Builds the runtime for nine invalid exporter and interval values, then records three times the queue size of calls against a collector that never answers, then closes the runtime, then disables both signals.
then: Expects every invalid setting refused, the calls not delayed, the export failures counted, shutdown inside one shared limit, and no provider for a disabled signal.

title: An invalid service name is refused and never echoed
when: Builds the runtime with a service name that holds a newline, with a 129-byte name and with a name that holds an equals sign.
then: Expects every name refused and the value absent from the error text.

title: An action deadline is reported and its workers are joined
when: Runs the controller with a 5 ms action timeout and an action that waits for its context.
then: Expects the observed reconcile_failed error to be context.DeadlineExceeded, and expects the scans to stop before Run returns.

title: A new event cannot bypass a failed key's retry delay
when: Fails one key, adds it 1,000 times, takes a healthy key, and then takes the failed key after its delay.
then: Expects the unchanged due time, progress for the healthy key, the retry only after its due time, and a delay that grows to the configured cap.

title: The emitted metadata lists only the top-level collections
when: Generates a service with scoped and unscoped collections and reads the emitted metadata body.
then: Expects kind API, the service name, the base path, and one entry for each unscoped collection only.

title: The emitted CORS middleware reads the environment and answers a preflight
when: Generates with CORS enabled and reads the emitted middleware.
then: Expects the allow-origin, allow-methods and allow-headers values read from the environment with defaults, and a 204 answer for an OPTIONS preflight.

title: The emitted routes serve exactly the declared base path
when: Registers the emitted route patterns for several literal base paths on a real multiplexer and sends requests.
then: Expects each declared path served and each neighbouring path unmatched.

title: The emitted handlers set the JSON content type
when: Reads each emitted handler.
then: Expects the application/json content type set before each successful body is encoded.

title: A before slot refusal becomes a problem response with its own code
when: Generates a collection with a bound before slot and reads the emitted handler.
then: Expects the slot status mapped to a problem response through errorForStatus, with the matching error code, and no store call.

title: A bound before-delete slot gates the delete
when: Generates a collection with a bound before-delete slot.
then: Expects the slot called with the record identity and the caller before the store delete, and the delete skipped on refusal.

title: An unbound slot is never called
when: Generates a collection with no slot bindings and with partial bindings.
then: Expects every slot call wrapped in a nil guard so an unbound slot passes the request through.

title: Every before slot has its own nil guard
when: Generates each before slot in turn.
then: Expects a nil guard for each one.

title: Every after slot has its own nil guard
when: Generates each after slot in turn.
then: Expects a nil guard for each one.

title: Keyed workers keep independent progress and serialize each key
when: Runs a keyed watch controller with two workers and repeated events for two keys.
then: Expects at most one active action for each key, and concurrent progress for the other key.

title: The emitted wiring registers one literal method-and-pattern route per operation
when: Generates a collection with every operation and reads the wiring.
then: Expects one mux registration per operation whose pattern is a method and a path string literal.

title: Route validation requires the current HTTP pattern rules
when: Checks the emitted route patterns while a legacy pattern mode is active.
then: Expects validation to refuse to run rather than accept an unchecked pattern.

title: An after-create slot runs after the store call
when: Generates a collection with a bound after-create slot and reads the emitted handler.
then: Expects the slot called with the persisted fields after the store create returned without error.

title: An after-delete slot runs after the store call
when: Generates a collection with a bound after-delete slot.
then: Expects the slot called with the record identity after the store delete returned without error.

title: Every emitted handler answers an error through the problem serializer
when: Reads each emitted handler.
then: Expects every error path to call handleError instead of writing its own body.

title: The emitted problem names the request path
when: Reads the emitted handleError function.
then: Expects the instance member set from the request path.

title: The emitted problem carries a UTC timestamp
when: Reads the emitted handleError function.
then: Expects the timestamp member set to the current UTC time in RFC 3339 form.

title: The error code prefix comes from the service name
when: Generates services whose names carry the common suffixes and hyphens.
then: Expects the prefix stripped, joined and upper-cased in every emitted error code.

title: Without a declared base the problem type is about:blank
when: Generates without an error type base.
then: Expects about:blank as the type in every constructor.

title: A validation problem carries its per-field array
when: Reads the emitted validation constructor.
then: Expects a validation_errors array of field and message pairs, omitted when empty.

title: A pending result keeps its capacity and its delay
when: Finishes one key with a one-hour recheck, adds that key again three times, restarts the queue, and then fills the capacity.
then: Expects no retry count for the pending key, the same due time after the events and the restart, an overflow error at the capacity bound, and progress for another key.

title: The emitted presenter adds the envelope metadata
when: Reads the emitted presentEntity helper.
then: Expects it to add id, kind and href to the entity members.

title: Each list item is presented like a single resource
when: Generates in envelope mode and reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects each item passed through presentEntity with its own identifier and resolved href.

title: Envelope mode declares the identifier dependency
when: Generates in envelope mode with a create operation and reads the wiring.
then: Expects the pinned identifier module required, and bare mode requiring none.

title: The emitted list handler parses every list parameter
when: Reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects the page, page size, order, field selection and search parameters read and passed into the list options.

title: The order direction override is checked
when: Reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects a 400 answer for an order value other than asc or desc, and the override applied to each order entry.

title: The identifier stays in the field selection
when: Reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects id added to the selection when the request omits it, and the metadata members always kept.

title: A field selection removes the fields it did not name
when: Reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects each presented item reduced to the selected members plus id, kind and href.

title: The emitted document declares both upsert answers
when: Generates the OpenAPI document for an upsert collection.
then: Expects both the 201 and the 200 answer declared for the operation.

title: The emitted patch handler reads, merges and saves
when: Generates a patch collection and reads the emitted handler.
then: Expects the stored record read first, the supplied members merged onto it, and the whole record saved.

title: The server-managed field rule covers all four cases
when: Checks the field classifier for a computed field, a timestamp field, created_by, updated_by, generation and an ordinary field.
then: Expects the first five classified as server-managed and the last not.

title: The scanner checks a whole page before any effect
when: Returns six pages with an empty cursor, a repeated cursor, invalid UTF-8, an oversized cursor, too many items, and an empty continuation.
then: Expects ErrScanContract for each page and zero emitter calls.

title: The emitted upsert handler checks the kind and resets the server fields
when: Generates an upsert collection with server-managed fields.
then: Expects the kind checked, the server-managed fields cleared, and the create-side values set from the server.

title: A failed body check answers with a validation problem

title: The emitted upsert handler forces the implicit values

title: The emitted list handler filters on the implicit values

title: A slow stream cannot starve retained history

title: The emitted update handler checks the parent scope

title: The emitted patch handler checks the parent scope
when: Generates a scoped patch collection.

title: The emitted delete handler checks the parent scope
