title: The emitted discovery handler serves all three endpoints
when: Generates a basic service and reads the emitted discovery file.
then: Expects the three handler methods, the embedded document, the HTML page and the JSON and HTML content types.

title: Without a base path the discovery routes start at the root
when: Generates with no base path and reads the wiring.
then: Expects the document route at the root and the metadata route bound to the exact root pattern.

title: The emitted document paths start at the base path
when: Generates with a base path and reads the emitted document.
then: Expects every declared path prefixed with that base path.

title: The emitted scalar response mappings convert, bound and own their values
when: Builds a project from the emitted responses package and runs its checks for presence, ownership, invalid values and integer bounds.
then: Expects a conversion error with no response for an invalid value, every valid value unchanged, and each result owned by the response.

title: The emitted nullable response mappings keep presence and refuse invalid values
when: Runs the emitted nullable conversions for an absent pointer, a present pointer, a zero value and out-of-range numbers.
then: Expects the declared presence policy applied, each value owned, and no response for an invalid value.

title: The emitted JSON object conversion bounds its input and owns its output
when: Runs the emitted object conversions for presence, exact numbers, ownership, invalid input and each declared bound.
then: Expects the declared bounds held, numbers not rounded, maps and lists unshared, and no partial response for invalid input.

title: The emitted JSON list conversion keeps its values and refuses invalid input
when: Runs the emitted list conversions for presence, invalid input and ownership.
then: Expects the list values kept, each list owned, and no partial list for invalid input.

title: The emitted process keeps its failure record fixed and private
when: Runs the generated process as a subprocess for a signal, a callback failure, three panic forms, a runtime.Goexit and a panic in a defer.
then: Expects exit code 1 with one fixed failure record for each fault, no private credential and no goroutine dump in the output, the cleanup marker written, and a clean exit after SIGTERM.

title: The emitted prepared inputs use the application values and own their output
when: Runs the emitted conversions with prepared application inputs beside the stored model.
then: Expects the prepared values used, their presence kept, each result owned, and invalid values refused.

title: The emitted enum conversion accepts only declared values
when: Runs the emitted enum conversions for declared values, presence and an unknown value.
then: Expects declared values kept with their presence, each value owned, and a conversion error with no response for an unknown value.

title: The emitted client refuses a call beyond its capacity
when: Holds the maximum number of requests open and starts one more.
then: Expects the extra call refused instead of queued, and capacity released when the held calls finish.

title: The emitted client reads only a private credential file
when: Reads a projected credential file at each permitted mode and at wider modes, then builds clients from invalid base URLs.
then: Expects only the four private modes accepted and every invalid base URL refused.

title: The emitted stream is bounded and cancellable
when: Streams a live frame then cancels, then streams over-large frames, over-large totals, a redirect, a foreign origin, an escaping path and a missing callback.
then: Expects the live frame delivered before cancellation and every unbounded or unsafe stream refused.

title: Closing the emitted client stops a live stream
when: Closes the client from inside a stream callback.
then: Expects the stream to end with an error promptly.

title: A certificate pin is copied and does not replace CA trust
when: Supplies an exact pin, a pin changed after construction, a different pin, no CA file, a wrong host name and an all-zero pin.
then: Expects the exact and copied pins accepted, the other cases refused without reaching the service, and the all-zero pin refused at construction.

title: The emitted order parser accepts only declared fields
when: Parses a valid two-entry order, then an unknown name, an injected statement, extra words, a trailing comma, a duplicate name, two aliases of one column and over-long input.
then: Expects the valid order mapped to its columns and directions and every other input refused.

title: An emitted empty-status endpoint writes no body
when: Builds endpoints for status 202, 204 and 205 over a real connection and sends verified, denied and unauthenticated requests.
then: Expects no body and no content type, no-store on every answer, the domain not reached for an unauthenticated request, and construction refused for a body response type at 204 and 205.

title: An emitted dynamic reply fails closed on a wrong status and body pair
when: Returns each combination of status and body from a reply endpoint.
then: Expects 202 and 200 with a body, 204 and 205 without one, and a 500 answer for every other combination.

title: A mutual-TLS publication requires every replica and keeps the message identity
when: Publishes one record with a 0440 private key behind a projected link, and then consumes it from the broker fixture.
then: Expects Acks of -1 in the produce request, the same payload, the resource key as the record key, and the message ID and kind as headers.

title: An emitted preparation callback runs once, in order, under the deadline
when: Sends a bad token, an undecodable request, a failing callback and a valid request, then builds endpoints with a nil callback and with two callbacks.
then: Expects the callback skipped for a token or decoding failure, run once with the verified identity and the request deadline otherwise, its failure kept apart from an authentication failure, and both invalid configurations refused.

title: A required member must be present but may be a zero value
when: Decodes bodies with zero values, explicit nulls, absent members, an empty nested object, an unknown tag value and untagged fields.
then: Expects zero values accepted, every absent or null required member refused, an unknown tag value reported as a configuration error, and untagged fields unchanged.

title: A cancelled request stops the emitted body read
when: Cancels the request context while the endpoint reads a partial body from a pipe.
then: Expects the handler to return promptly with status 503.

title: A cancelled socket request stops the emitted body read
when: Cancels the server context while the endpoint reads a partial body from a real socket.
then: Expects status 503 on that connection.

title: The emitted projector checks a selector without reading data
when: Parses unknown paths, over-deep paths, invalid wildcards, empty terms, duplicates, wrong case, over-long input and control bytes, then overlapping parent and child paths.
then: Expects every invalid selector refused with the request error, and an overlapping selection giving the same result in any order.

title: The emitted projector refuses a malformed list response
when: Projects null, arrays, missing item arrays, non-object items, duplicate members, bad Unicode, trailing values, over-long arrays and an over-large encoded value.
then: Expects the projection error for each one and for a zero selection.

title: The emitted projector bounds data the caller did not select
when: Projects one selected field from items that exceed the member, element and depth limits in their unselected parts.
then: Expects the projection error in each case.

title: The emitted projector copies its schema and is safe to share
when: Builds projectors from invalid, cyclic and over-wide schemas, then widens a schema after construction, then projects from many goroutines.
then: Expects each invalid schema refused, the later change ignored, and no undeclared data exposed under concurrent use.

title: An unselected list keeps the normal response path
when: Calls the optional projector with no selection, with a selection, with a zero selection and with an invalid item field name.
then: Expects the original value returned unchanged and unencoded for no selection, the projected bytes for a selection, and the projection error for the two invalid cases.

title: The emitted timestamp conversion refuses an out-of-range instant without output
when: Converts instants before the first and after the last protobuf instant, negative and large years, and zoned boundary instants, through both the required and the optional function.
then: Expects no output and the fixed timestamp error with no supplied value in its text.

title: An unverified broker connection is refused
when: Connects to a broker with a wrong host name, then a wrong trust root, then a wrong client certificate, then no TLS.
then: Expects every connection refused, with valid client options in each case.

title: The emitted optional timestamp keeps presence and owns its output
when: Converts a nil pointer, then the same present zero time twice, then mutates the input and one result.
then: Expects absence kept, present zero kept, two separate results, and neither result changed by the mutations.

title: The emitted timestamp conversion drops the monotonic clock and the local zone
when: Converts the current time.
then: Expects the wall-clock instant unchanged and the result in UTC.

title: The emitted response mapping owns its output and keeps absence
when: Maps a stored model, then mutates the source and one result, then maps a model with absent optional values.
then: Expects the results unshared and unchanged by the mutations, and each absent value still absent.

title: The emitted response mapping refuses an invalid value without a partial message
when: Maps models with invalid encodings, out-of-range numbers, out-of-range instants and JSON lists beyond their declared bounds.
then: Expects no message and the fixed conversion error for each one.

title: A prepared mapping uses the application values, not the stored ones
when: Maps a stored row together with prepared scalar, timestamp, pointer and JSON inputs, then repeats it with the optional inputs absent.
then: Expects every prepared value in the result, field presence kept for a present empty value, and each absent optional input still absent.

title: A prepared mapping refuses an invalid supplied value
when: Maps prepared inputs with invalid encodings, out-of-range numbers and instants, and over-bound JSON lists.
then: Expects no message and the fixed conversion error, with no supplied value in the error.

title: A prepared registrar keeps the other registrations unchanged
when: Registers one service through a prepared registrar and another through the plain registrar, then calls both.
then: Expects the callback to run for the prepared service only, after verification and decoding, and the shared descriptors unchanged.

title: The emitted probe command is bounded and does no domain work
when: Validates monitor addresses, runs the probe command with valid and invalid arguments, and probes servers that return a long body, a redirect, a wrong status and no answer.
then: Expects only a loopback address with a canonical port accepted, the domain never opened, unknown arguments refused, and each bad answer refused within its bound.

title: A monitor that cannot bind fails the process before Open
when: Runs the process with the monitor address already in use.
then: Expects a failed process and no call to the domain Open function.

title: A failed start still produces correlated signals and a fixed failure event
when: Runs the emitted executable for an Open error, an Open panic and an Open goroutine exit against a TLS collector.
then: Expects the telemetry runtime present in the initialization context, the fixed failure event emitted before telemetry closes, no private values in the signals, and a non-zero exit.

title: SCRAM authenticates over TLS and keeps the password private
when: Publishes with SCRAM-SHA-512 over TLS from a password file, then repeats with a wrong password.
then: Expects the first publication to succeed, the second connection to fail, and no password text in the error.

title: Cleanup keeps its flush and its bound after a failing callback
when: Runs the emitted executable for a restart, a registration error, a cleanup error, a cleanup panic and a cleanup goroutine exit.
then: Expects the remaining cleanup and the telemetry flush kept, the exact stop and failure event counts, and shutdown inside its limit.

title: The emitted store keeps old sessions readable across a key rollout
when: Reads one old record through four key rings, writes through two mixed writers, then signs out during a key switch.
then: Expects every listed key to decrypt, the first key to encrypt new records, a removed key to lose access, and a renewal after sign-out to fail.

title: A storage failure reports temporary unavailability and keeps the cookie
when: Closes the database, then asks for the session.
then: Expects 503 with Retry-After 1 and no Set-Cookie header.

title: The emitted callback consumes a pending login exactly once
when: Sends a callback with a wrong state, then sends the same valid callback from two backend instances at the same time.
then: Expects no code exchange for the wrong state, one success and one denial for the concurrent pair, and exactly one exchange.

title: A rejected identity token gets no session and is revoked
when: Completes a callback for eight provider modes with a bad nonce, issuer, audience, expiry, issue time, auth time, roles or access token hash.
then: Expects 502 for each mode, no session cookie, and eight token revocations.

title: A rejected API session returns the fixed reauthentication response
when: Sends an API request with no session, then with a session the upstream rejects, then repeats it.
then: Expects the fixed 401 body, the WWW-Authenticate and no-store headers, no forwarded Location or ETag, a cleared cookie, and one upstream call.

title: The completion document keeps the strict cookie and holds no private state
when: Completes a protected application callback, then replays the same callback.
then: Expects a Strict, Secure, HttpOnly, host-only cookie, no session ID, token, code or state in the body, and 400 with no document for the replay.

title: Each index document gets a fresh style nonce
when: Requests the index document three times with dynamic styles enabled, then an asset, then an invalid insertion offset.
then: Expects three distinct 32-byte nonces that match their own document and policy, a changed ETag each time, no nonce on the asset, and a closed failure for the bad offset.

title: The runtime refuses a changed grant on its session table
when: Adds a schema CREATE grant, adds a grant option, and removes the DELETE grant.
then: Expects both Verify and Bootstrap to refuse each case.

title: Schema setup is locked, repeatable and limited to data access
when: Runs two owner connections through Bootstrap at the same time, repeats the setup, then runs data and schema statements as the runtime login.
then: Expects both owners to succeed, an unchanged catalog snapshot after the repeat, the four data statements to pass, and four schema statements to be denied.

title: An unbounded SCRAM challenge is refused before key derivation
when: Gives the bounded session six challenges with too many iterations, too few iterations, a repeated field, a missing field and an oversized body.
then: Expects each challenge refused, with no call to the inner session.

title: Startup refuses a schema that differs from the generated one
when: Changes the table, a column, a constraint or an index, then verifies the schema.
then: Expects the runtime to refuse startup for each change.

title: Schema setup refuses invalid input
when: Calls Verify and Bootstrap with a nil context, a nil connection and an unsafe role name.
then: Expects the fixed schema error for each call.

title: The inserted runtime metadata is escaped and changes no policy
when: Requests the index document before and after the telemetry service name is set, with the earlier ETag.
then: Expects a fresh response, the escaped stego-runtime-config element, a disabled export for a missing collector, and the same content security policy.

title: The authorization request keeps the declared scopes
when: Starts login with one declared scope and then with four declared scopes.
then: Expects the authorization request's scope parameter to equal the declared value each time.

title: An API permission denial does not end a valid session
when: Makes the upstream API answer 403, then 401.
then: Expects the session to stay authenticated after the 403 and to end after the 401.

title: The pending login limit is enforced
when: Inserts 1,000 pending logins with one bounded statement, then creates one more.
then: Expects the store error and exactly 1,000 remaining records.

title: A cross-site request cannot read a private response
when: Sends the public page and three private routes with a cross-site and then a same-site fetch site, holding a valid cookie.
then: Expects 200 for the public page and 403 for the session, login and API routes.

title: The emitted JSON reader accepts only strict documents
when: Reads seven invalid documents with a repeated name, a lone surrogate, trailing data or deep nesting, then three valid documents.
then: Expects every invalid document refused and every valid document accepted.

title: The application upstream address stays compiler-owned
when: Starts the backend with a plaintext upstream, a foreign upstream and an unused trust file from the service environment.
then: Expects a compiler-owned error for each attempt.

title: The proxy passes an upstream cache response through
when: Makes the upstream answer 304 and sends a conditional API request.
then: Expects 304, an empty body and the upstream ETag.

title: An uncertain produce closes its client before the next call
when: Blocks the produce request until a 100 ms deadline expires, then releases the broker and publishes again.
then: Expects context.DeadlineExceeded, a prompt return, a different client for the next call, and a successful publication.

title: Telemetry ingest needs a session, an origin, a CSRF token and protobuf
when: Sends seven ingest requests with a missing session, missing CSRF token, missing Origin, wrong media type, wrong method, unknown path or oversize body, then a browser bearer token and compressed input.
then: Expects the stated status for each case and expects no telemetry at the API.

title: Telemetry admission bounds the burst and the session map
when: Takes six admissions for one session, then one more, then fills the session map and asks for another session.
then: Expects the six admissions, the refusal after them, and a 512-entry bound on the map.

title: Socket admission bounds each session and each backend
when: Takes two sockets for one session and then a third, ends the session, fills the backend capacity, then closes the set.
then: Expects the busy error for the third session socket, the cancellation on end, the busy error at backend capacity, and no socket after close.

title: A socket upgrade needs a session and an exact origin
when: Dials the socket route without a session, with a wrong Origin, with no Origin, with a browser bearer token, and with a denied query.

title: A socket survives the HTTP deadlines and relays both message kinds
when: Opens a socket through a server with 80 ms deadlines, waits 120 ms, then relays a binary and a text message and ends the session.
then: Expects both messages returned without a change, the exit status in the close reason, and a 101 upgrade status in the telemetry wrapper.

title: Every session end closes that session's sockets
when: Ends the session through local sign-out, remote sign-out, backend close, runtime stop, a storage failure, session expiry and token expiry.
then: Expects the socket to close in each mode and expects no socket lease to remain.

title: The socket data budget counts messages, bytes and empty frames
when: Offers data at the message bound, at the byte bound, an empty message at the last slot, and one oversize message.
then: Expects a refusal at each bound, the empty message counted, and the oversize message refused.

title: A stalled export reaches its deadline and a terminal result
when: Replaces the transport with a fetch that never settles, records one span and flushes.
then: Expects the flush to fail inside 6.5 seconds and a reported trace failure, so the export does not wait without a bound.

title: The emitted runtime holds its log, instrument and attribute limits
when: Emits a log body of 513 characters and an object log body, creates 33 counters, then adds a value with a 257-character attribute.
then: Expects no log export, two invalid_record reports for logs and two for metrics, so the limits refuse the records before export.

title: Observable metric callbacks use the direct write limits and release their capacity
when: Registers the same callback twice on an observable gauge, counter and up-down counter, observes one valid value, an oversized attribute, an array attribute and an infinite value, then removes each registration.
then: Expects three collections for three instruments, nine invalid_record reports, the valid series exported, the oversized and array attributes absent from the payload, and no further collection after removal.

title: Invalid configuration, secret modes and payloads fail before the network
when: Gives nine invalid configurations, four unsafe secret file modes, four private modes, an invalid trust file and four invalid payloads.
then: Expects every invalid configuration, unsafe mode, invalid trust file and invalid payload refused, and the four private modes accepted.

title: Public deployment metadata controls each exporter
when: Supplies no metadata element, then an all-off element, then an element with traces and metrics on, then an out-of-range ratio, then an element with an extra key.
then: Expects exports only for the single valid element and only for its enabled signals, and no export for absent or invalid metadata.

title: Server rendering creates no browser transport
when: Removes the page location, then records a span, a log and a metric and runs flush and shutdown.
then: Expects no fetch call at all, so the server render creates no exporter, provider or timer.

title: A hidden page flushes and shutdown happens once
when: Records one span, raises a page-hide event, calls shutdown twice, then raises the event again.
then: Expects the trace export after the first event, the same result object for both shutdown calls, and no further call after shutdown, so the listeners are removed.

title: Batch observable callbacks observe only their own selection
when: Registers a batch callback for another meter's instrument, then for a synchronous instrument, then one valid callback that observes its selected instrument, an unselected instrument and a foreign instrument after an await.
then: Expects the two invalid registrations never called, four invalid_record reports, and only the selected instrument observed.

title: The emitted apply command keeps a dry run local and keeps exact integers
when: Runs a dry run of two documents with the configuration path moved to an absent file, then applies the same documents, then applies them again.
then: Expects the validated status with no API call and no credential read, a created status for each new resource, the large integer stored with its exact value, and a configured status with the same ID for the repeated apply.

title: The emitted apply command never changes an immutable resource
when: Applies one immutable membership manifest against a TLS API for a new resource, a manifest without a name, an existing exact match, a create conflict, a conflict with different fields, an ambiguous list, a wrong row, a wrong write answer and a denied read.
then: Expects the escaped identity query with page size two, POST as the only write method, the created or unchanged status for each accepted case, the unchanged status and no write for a repeat, no write after a lookup failure, an error for each mismatch, and no token in the output.

title: The emitted CLI converts a relative duration before any request
when: Sends day and hour durations through the relative flag against a TLS server, then an absolute value, then a body file, then conflicting, zero, negative and overflowing values with an output file selected.
then: Expects one absolute RFC 3339 timestamp inside the command interval, unchanged absolute and body values, every invalid or conflicting value refused with no request, no reserved output file, and the relative flag in the help text.

title: The emitted version command works without configuration
when: Runs the version command with the configuration path set to an absent file, then runs it with an extra argument, then declares a command named version beside the built-in one.
then: Expects a JSON object with exactly the application and compiler records, a valid compiler record, an error and no output for the extra argument, and a refused declaration of the reserved name.

title: An uncertain refresh keeps its pending state and the session identity
when: Saves an expired OIDC session, then lets the provider return a changed subject, and separately makes the configuration directory read-only during the token request, then requests credentials again with a correct provider.
then: Expects no credential from the failed refresh, exactly one provider refresh across both attempts, a refusal of the second attempt, and the pending record still in the saved session.

title: A foreign, unidentified, conflicted or denied resource is never adopted, and an invalid desired object never reaches the API.
when: Ensure and DeleteOwned run against four stored resources (foreign labels, no identity, a 409 conflict and a 403 denial), then Ensure runs with five invalid desired objects and DeleteOwned runs with empty owner labels.
then: Every call fails, the foreign and unidentified resources receive no write at all, and each invalid desired object and the empty owner are refused before any request.

title: The emitted search engine binds every value, quotes every column and holds its input limits
when: Parses 13 valid searches, nine invalid searches, and many concurrent searches on one engine.
then: Expects the exact parenthesized SQL with quoted columns, a parameter for each value, the exact numeric text, FALSE and TRUE for the empty lists, a refusal for each unknown field and each limit, and no fault under concurrent use.

title: A replaced token file takes effect on the next request and a world-readable token file is refused.
when: The client makes a request, the test writes a new token to the same file, the client makes another request, and then the test changes the file mode to 0644.
then: The server sees the new bearer token without a client restart, and the request after the mode change fails before it reaches the server.

title: A large integer keeps its exact value and a response that is not one JSON object is refused.
when: The server returns the integer 9007199254740993, then null, then an array, then two objects in one body.
then: The decoded value keeps its exact text and matches the exact int64 but not the neighbouring value, and each of the three other bodies returns an error.

title: An inconsistent, repeated or denied list snapshot never becomes a baseline.
when: One observation cycle runs against a server that changes the list resource version between pages, repeats an object UID, repeats a cursor, denies the list, or denies only the watch.
then: Each case returns an error, no REPLACE reaches the consumer except in the watch-denied case where the list was complete, and both denial cases return ErrWatchAccess.

title: An invalid collection path makes no request and a consumer error stops observation.
when: Observe runs with an absolute URL, a dot-dot path, a percent-encoded dot-dot path, a path that carries a query, and a path with an empty segment, then with a consumer that returns an error.
then: No invalid path reaches the server, and the consumer's own error comes back from Observe.

title: An empty page keeps its objects and an oversized snapshot is stopped before it becomes a baseline.
when: The server returns a first empty page and then one object, or an endless run of cursors, or an endless run of full 100-object pages.
then: The empty-page case still delivers the one object in its REPLACE, the two endless cases return an error with no REPLACE and no retained cursor, and the page count stays inside the page bound.

title: A rate-limited response carries its retry delay as bounded status metadata and no response body.
when: The server answers 429 with a Retry-After header of 120 and a private body, and the delay parser then reads a negative value, an invalid value, 999999 seconds, one second and an HTTP date.
then: The error holds only the method, the status 429 and a two-minute delay, and the parser returns zero for the invalid inputs and caps the delay at one hour.

title: The public failure summary reports only a known method and a valid status.
when: The summary reads a plain error that holds a private value, an API error with an unknown method, an API error with an out-of-range status, a wrapped API error, and nil.
then: The first three return the fixed text, the wrapped error keeps only its method and status, and nil returns an empty string.

title: API discovery reads one bounded response and fails closed on any missing or changed requirement.
when: The requirement check runs for a core path, a grouped path, and eleven answers that are missing, partial, of the wrong group version, kind or namespace scope, short of a verb, duplicated, malformed, denied or unavailable.
then: Each run makes exactly one request, the valid and core answers pass, the HTTP failures keep their status metadata, and every other answer returns ErrDiscovery.

title: An invalid group version or resource requirement is refused before any request.
when: The requirement check runs with seven invalid group versions and seven invalid requirement sets, including a subresource name, a missing verb list, a repeated verb, an unknown verb and 33 entries.
then: Every call returns ErrDiscovery and the fake server records no request.

title: Discovery reads the API and the token again for each call, so removed support cannot stay cached.
when: The requirement check passes once, then the token file is replaced and the server stops reporting the resource, and the check runs again.
then: The second call uses the new bearer token and returns ErrDiscovery instead of the earlier success.

title: A group reads each declared name once and uses its declared defaults
when: Reads one group with a lookup that counts its calls and supplies one variable, then reads a second group.
then: Expects the declared defaults for the absent fields, five lookups with one call each, and no cross-group read.

title: A computed patch uses only its original observation and is never retried or widened.
when: PatchOwned sends a change computed from an earlier read against a server that answers 409, then runs with five patches that hold a system field or no field, two wrong observed paths, and foreign owner labels.
then: The server sees exactly one PATCH that carries the original UID and resource version, the conflict comes back unretried, the caller's two input objects are unchanged, and every invalid call is refused before any further request.

title: Route admission accepts only the selected passthrough backend and keeps pending separate from invalid.
when: The admission check reads four valid Routes, nine pending Routes, twenty-two invalid Routes covering path routing, a wildcard policy, an alternate backend, a zero weight, router TLS data and conflicting ingress entries, and seven invalid host requirements.
then: The valid Routes pass, each pending Route returns false without an error, and every invalid Route or host requirement returns ErrResourceObservation.

title: The trust parser accepts only certificate blocks and keeps a private copy of the pool.
when: The parser reads a one-certificate bundle and a two-certificate bundle, the test then clears the input bytes and verifies a leaf again, and the parser then reads ten invalid inputs including a private key, leading and trailing text, a malformed prefix and PEM headers.
then: Verification still succeeds after the input is cleared, and every invalid input returns ErrResourceObservation with a nil pool.

title: Client TLS Secret verification shares the Secret boundary and refuses a server-only certificate.
when: The client verifier reads a valid owned Secret with a client certificate, the same invalid variants as the server verifier, three invalid targets, an expired certificate, and a certificate that permits only server use.
then: Only the valid client certificate passes, and every other case returns ErrResourceObservation with no returned data and no added error text.

title: The rollout digest follows Secret names and data and ignores resource metadata.
when: The digest is computed for two owned Secrets, then after a resource version change, then after a data change, then after a rename, then with the data supplied as a plain decoded map.
then: The metadata change keeps the digest, the data change and the rename each change it, and the decoded map produces the same digest as the generated object type.

title: An unowned, inactive, mistyped or oversized Secret set has no digest.
when: The digest is computed for nineteen invalid sets covering a foreign owner, a missing UID or version, a wrong namespace, name, kind, API version or type, a deleting Secret, an invalid data key or value, non-canonical base64, the entry and total size bounds, and duplicate names, then for an invalid namespace, an empty set, a short set and a missing owner.
then: Every case returns ErrResourceObservation or an error with an empty digest.

title: The Secret set operation validates the whole set, requires exactly the stored data, and reads each Secret again.
when: The operation runs in twelve modes against a fake API server, including an injected extra data key, changed data or a replaced UID on the second read, a removed Secret, a foreign owner, a lost identity, a conflict, an invalid second desired Secret, a stringData field and a canceled context.
then: The valid mode creates both Secrets, a repeated call writes nothing, rotation writes exactly one Secret, the caller's input is unchanged, every other mode fails with an empty digest and no Secret data in the error, and an invalid second Secret or a canceled context reaches no API call.

title: Registry credential JSON is accepted only as auths data for the exact selected registries.
when: The validator reads eighteen invalid inputs covering an empty body, the size bound, trailing data, a credential helper, an unknown field, a foreign or wildcard registry, repeated member names, an empty user or password, a control character, non-canonical base64 and invalid UTF-8, then nine invalid registry selections, then a valid input twice with the registries in both orders.
then: Every invalid input and selection returns ErrImagePullSecret, the valid input passes, and the selection order does not change the produced content.

title: An assignment change adds and removes watches and restarts only the namespace whose identity changed.
when: The set runs with two namespace scopes, then an assignment that drops one and adds another, then an assignment that gives one namespace a new identity, then an empty assignment.
then: The dropped scope's watch closes and produces REMOVED, the unchanged scope keeps its watch, the changed identity closes and joins the old watch before the replacement starts and delivers a baseline, and the empty assignment closes both remaining watches.

title: An invalid or oversized assignment is refused without disturbing the running watches.
when: One scope runs with a collection limit of one, then Replace receives nine invalid scopes covering cluster-wide paths, an object path, a subresource path, a dot-dot segment, a query, a percent-encoded name, an empty namespace and an empty identity, then a two-scope assignment, then a canceled context.
then: Each invalid scope and the oversized assignment return ErrWatchSetContract, the canceled call returns context.Canceled, and the existing watch stays open until the final empty assignment closes it.

title: An invalid value returns the zero settings and a private error
when: Reads the group with 18 invalid inputs, which cover a missing value, an explicitly empty value, control characters, invalid UTF-8, string length, integer spelling and bounds, duration bounds and length, and boolean spelling, and then with a nil lookup.
then: Expects the zero settings value and ErrConfiguration for each input, an error that names the group, the field and a fixed reason, and no input text in any format of the error.

title: A denied scope is reported once and retried only after a new assignment.
when: One scope is assigned while the server denies every read, the set reports the failure, access is then allowed, and the same scope is assigned again.
then: The denial produces RESET with ErrWatchAccess and no empty baseline, the server records exactly one call until the new assignment arrives, and the retry then delivers a complete baseline.

title: An aggregate object or byte limit, or an object from another namespace, stops the whole set.
when: Two namespace scopes are assigned with an aggregate object limit of one, with a byte limit just under two objects, or against a server that returns an object labelled with a foreign namespace.
then: Each case stops Run with ErrWatchSetContract, at most one baseline reaches the consumer, and the foreign-object case delivers no baseline at all.

title: Only one complete list runs at a time and a removal waits for its watch to stop.
when: Two scopes are assigned against an observer whose first list blocks until the test releases it, then both baselines complete, then an empty assignment removes both scopes.
then: The second list does not start while the first holds the baseline slot, both scopes deliver a baseline after the release, and Replace returns only after both watch workers have stopped.

title: Durable Secret state is created once, withheld until its pin and binding match, and never replaced.
when: The helper creates the Secret and its immutable marker, waits for the allocator to copy the digest to the namespace annotation, registers the binding, and then runs again after a removed Secret or marker, changed data, a changed pin, lost owner labels, a closed binding, a replaced namespace, or invalid prepared data.
then: The first call returns ErrSecretStatePending and writes only the Secret and the marker, the second call registers the digest once, every damaged case fails without a new write or initialization, and the recover and read-only cases return the same Secret.

title: An ownership read still works while every configured watch stream is open.
when: Sixteen namespace watches start and stay open on one client whose watch limit is sixteen, and the test then reads a namespace through the same client.
then: Each watch starts on its own namespace path with its credential, the namespace read returns 200 with the expected UID, and cancellation stops all sixteen watches with an error.

title: A browser deployment matches the API deployment byte for byte and refuses a gRPC ingress peer
when: The generator runs once for a rest-api declaration and once for the equivalent browser-backend declaration, and then the browser declaration adds an ingress peer on port 9090.
then: Both file sets have the same length, and each file has the same path and the same bytes. The declaration with the 9090 ingress peer is refused.

title: The RPC Deployment keeps one replica and the selected rollout strategy
when: The test renders the RPC manifest for the default declaration, then for an explicit RollingUpdate choice and an explicit Recreate choice.
then: Each Deployment uses one replica. The default and the explicit RollingUpdate strategy use one extra Pod and zero unavailable Pods. Recreate carries no rolling-update settings. The file set, the file paths and every other resource stay equal to the default output.

title: The RPC image and manifest carry the declared process, its TLS listener and its loopback monitor
when: The generator writes the files for one declared RPC process twice.
then: Both passes write the same bytes. The RPC Containerfile builds the declared process path and declares the explicit entry point. The RPC manifest names its own service account, both probe modes, the loopback monitor address, the gRPC listen address and the TLS key path.

title: A profile without a runtime class emits no runtime-class admission rule
when: An isolated profile declares an account and network isolation but no Pod runtime class, and the test reads every generated object.
then: The profile keeps the isolated security mode with an empty runtime class. No generated policy names runtimeClassName. The number of generated policies does not change.

title: Only the assigned network node identity can change the Pod network output annotation
when: The test compiles the generated rule for the OVN key and for the Multus key, then evaluates it for each request case.
then: The rule permits the assigned node to add, change or remove its own output through a status update, and permits a create request and an ordinary update that preserve the value. It denies a workload write, another node, a spoofed username prefix, a wrong or missing group, another subresource, a main-resource write, a create injection, a changed node assignment and a missing assignment.

title: A settings value is redacted and cannot be exported
when: Formats a complete settings value, a pointer to it, a slice of it and a map of it in five formats, and then marshals each one to JSON.
then: Expects no field value in any format, and a failed JSON export.

title: An omitted profile field stays an explicit null and survives the API response format
when: The declaration omits the container arguments, the environment, the mounts, the volumes and the dependencies, and the test then adds one empty environment value and reads the full widget mounts.
then: The Pod holds a present null for its volume and pull-Secret fields. The container holds a present null for its argument, environment and mount fields. An empty environment value and a false mount flag still match after the upstream omit rules serialize them.

title: The local application proxy drops every untrusted browser header
when: Sends authenticated application requests, and a second backend's requests, with a cookie and four client-supplied identity headers.
then: Expects the server access token at the application, all five untrusted headers absent, and no private header in the response.

title: A local application write needs an exact origin and a trusted fetch site
when: Sends POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE with a missing, foreign or repeated Origin and with four fetch site values, then with a valid pair.
then: Expects 403 or 400 for every unsafe combination and 200 for the exact origin with a same-origin or absent fetch site.

title: An anonymous document request starts login and keeps the cookie
when: Requests an API path and an asset with no session, a declared route by direct navigation, then the landing page cross-site.
then: Expects 401 for the private paths, a 303 to the login route for the document, the sign-in page cross-site, and no Set-Cookie header.

title: A captured asset needs a session and stops after sign-out
when: Reads each captured path from two backends with a session, anonymously, conditionally, with a browser bearer token, then after sign-out.
then: Expects no-store and no token in every body, 401 for an anonymous read, 400 for the bearer token, and 401 on the second backend after sign-out.

title: Startup diagnostics name each stage and hold no private input
when: Runs the generated runtime in a child process for six failure points and one success, with private markers in every configuration value.
then: Expects one completion record per stage in order, the correct outcome for the last stage, only the ten permitted fields, and no private marker in the output.

title: A startup step keeps its error, its context and its panic
when: Runs a startup step for a nil error, a cancellation, a deadline and a private error, then one that panics.
then: Expects the same error value, exactly one call, the caller's own context, and the panic passed through unchanged.

title: A failed renewal claim leaves the session usable
when: Injects a lost row, a cancellation and a deadline at the claim read, then renews the session again.
then: Expects the store error, an active session with its original credentials, no refresh token use, and one successful later renewal.

title: A cancelled renewal leaves no refresh claim
when: Pauses the provider inside the renewal, then cancels the caller.
then: Expects the renewal to fail and expects no retained refresh claim in the store.

title: The emitted package and its declarations compile and run under strict checks
when: Writes the emitted files to a temporary project with the pinned dependencies, then runs the Node runtime fixture and compiles testdata/usage.mts with strict TypeScript, bounded target and NodeNext resolution.
then: Expects both commands to pass, so the emitted declarations describe the emitted runtime and a strict consumer compiles against them; the test does not call a detached lifecycle method.

title: The emitted middleware denies every unsafe token and keeps its denial response safe
when: Sends one signed token for each of twenty faults through the emitted middleware, and one valid token.
then: Expects 401 for every fault, 204 for the valid token, no claim from the verifier after a denial, and a denial response with no token, a WWW-Authenticate header and Cache-Control no-store.

title: The built CLI keeps clean stdout and records one private command completion
when: Builds the generated CLI with the tracing component, runs the version command, an unknown command named with a private prefix, and a read command against a stalled TLS server that it then stops with SIGTERM.
then: Expects valid JSON on stdout and diagnostics on stderr, empty stdout after cancellation, exactly one command completion record for each run with the success, failure and canceled outcome, an HTTP client completion inside the canceled run, and no private argument, command name or credential in the records; the deadline and aborted outcomes and the configuration path are not exercised.

title: No generated file carries the withdrawn pinned admission renderer.
when: The generator runs with a bound HTTP application peer and the test reads every emitted file path and body.
then: The output is not empty, no path names pinned_admission, and no file body contains PinnedAdmissionPolicies.

title: A consumer error stops the watch set and the same set can run again.
when: One scope is assigned twice in succession to the same watch set, and the consumer returns its own error for the first change each time.
then: Run returns that exact consumer error on both runs, which proves the set stops on the error and releases its session so a later Run can start.

title: An invalid or closed state binding is refused before any Kubernetes request.
when: The durable state helper loads five malformed bindings: closed without a digest, a digest with no presence, presence with no digest, presence with a non-hexadecimal digest, and presence that is also closed.
then: Every call fails with no returned Secret, the initialize callback never runs, and the fake API server records no request at all.

title: A patch is refused for a terminating resource and reports an absent resource as an error.
when: PatchOwned runs with correct owner labels against a server that answers 404, and then runs again after a deletionTimestamp is added to the same observation.
then: The 404 comes back as an error, the terminating observation is refused as well, and the server records exactly one request, so the terminating resource never reached the network.

title: The emitted verifier refuses weak trust settings and weak key material
when: Builds a verifier for each invalid configuration, then starts the middleware from a key file that is valid, malformed and oversize.
then: Expects a refusal for an empty configuration, a plaintext issuer, an absent audience, a small modulus and a wrong exponent, and a startup failure for a missing audience, a malformed key and an oversize key file.

title: The emitted verifier refuses ambiguous tokens and ambiguous header values
when: Verifies hand-signed tokens with a duplicate payload member, a duplicate header member, an array payload, 34 nesting levels and an oversize length, then sends four invalid header shapes.
then: Expects a refusal for every ambiguous token, and 401 for an absent, unprefixed, wrongly prefixed or repeated header value.

title: The emitted verifier exposes the verified profile and only the configured role claim
when: Verifies a token that holds profile claims, an unselected roles claim and the configured nested role array, then removes and corrupts that array.
then: Expects the verified issuer, subject, profile claims, expiry and selected roles, equal HTTP and shared-context identities, no role from another claim, and a failure for every malformed or oversize role value.

title: The emitted key set selects one exact key and refuses an invalid key document
when: Verifies a token against a key document, then changes one key field at a time, repeats a key ID, sends an oversize document, forges the signature, marks the key sign only, and rotates the key ID.
then: Expects the valid token accepted, every invalid field and document refused, the forged signature refused, no fallback to an unrelated key, and the rotated key accepted.

title: The emitted key source rotates, refuses an untrusted endpoint and fails closed after its outage window
when: Starts a key source against a TLS endpoint without and then with its CA, rotates the key document, holds the clock, fails the endpoint, recovers it, cancels a request and calls Stop twice.
then: Expects an untrusted certificate refused with no request sent, one request for each refresh, no refresh inside the cooldown, the rotated key accepted, the removed key denied, a known key valid for fifteen minutes only, recovery after the failure, no provider contact for a canceled request, and every request denied after Stop.

title: The emitted key source holds its input limits and refuses a redirect or a plaintext URL
when: Starts a key source from an empty, oversize and ambiguous key file, verifies an oversize token, then points the source at a redirecting TLS endpoint and at a plaintext URL.
then: Expects every invalid key file refused, the oversize token refused, the redirect refused with no request to the target, and the plaintext URL refused.

title: A startup error from the emitted key source holds no provider detail
when: Starts a key source against an endpoint that returns an oversize body, oversize headers and an error status with a private message.
then: Expects startup refused in each case, and the error text without the source address and without the provider message.

title: Key refresh telemetry holds no private data and records no work for a cache hit
when: Runs file and HTTPS key sources with the telemetry peer, forces a success, a failure, a recovery, a cooldown rejection, a stopped verifier, a canceled startup and an expired startup, and reads the local signal output.
then: Expects the five fixed outcomes in order, no further record, and no token, key ID, file path, source URL or issuer text in the output.

title: The emitted grant policy matches every authority dimension and denies when empty
when: Builds a policy from one grant, then asks it for an altered issuer, subject, resource, operation and target, for an admin role caller, for a nil policy and for a zero policy, and reads it from sixteen workers.
then: Expects the exact grant permitted, every altered dimension denied, the role ignored, the nil and zero policies denying, the constructor input copy unchanged, and concurrent reads stable.

title: The emitted SSO handler denies untrusted tokens, keeps its public paths exact and closes on Stop
when: Sends fourteen token cases through the handler, then requests each public path and each subpath, then calls Stop twice and repeats a valid request.
then: Expects 401 for a wrong issuer, a wrong audience, an absent expiry, an absent issuer, audience, subject or issue time, a future issue time, an expired token, a wrong signature, a wrong algorithm, a repeated header and an oversize token, 204 for the valid token only, a denial response with no token and both safety headers, 204 for each exact public path, 401 for each subpath, and 401 after Stop.

title: The emitted SSO handler maps claims in its declared order and grants no role
when: Verifies a token in the SSO, OIDC and name-fallback claim shapes.
then: Expects the username, first name, last name, email, client and issuer from the declared claim order, the mapped username as UserID, an empty Role and the retained verified expiry.

title: The emitted SSO handler refuses an unsafe startup
when: Starts the handler with no issuer, with no audience, with AUTH_ENABLED set to false, FALSE and invalid, and with a missing key file.
then: Expects every startup refused.

title: The emitted provider checks every service-account token claim against its saved policy
when: Verifies a signed service-account token for nineteen cases that change the issuer, the subject, the client, the audience set, the role arrays, the times, the lifetime, the expiry response, the signature and the key document.
then: Expects the valid token accepted and every other case refused, with an empty role policy accepting an absent or empty claim and refusing an explicit null.

title: The emitted provider refuses an unsafe grant and releases no credential for an unsafe client
when: Asks for a verified service-account secret for ten cases that add a refresh token, add an ID token, change the token type, make the client public or disabled, remove the subject, change the owner before and after the grant, and change the policy subject.
then: Expects the credential returned for the valid case only, no credential read or grant request for a public, disabled or subject-less client, and ErrOwnership with no grant when the owner changes.

title: The emitted provider refuses an unsafe browser callback before any provider request
when: Validates four safe callbacks and twenty-five unsafe callbacks, then creates a browser client with an empty callback, a foreign logout origin and a zero lifetime.
then: Expects the safe callbacks accepted, every unsafe callback refused, every invalid policy refused, and no provider request for an invalid policy.

title: The emitted provider builds a confidential PKCE browser client and refuses unsafe drift
when: Builds the desired browser configuration, then compares it with eleven drifted live records.
then: Expects a confidential, disabled client with the standard flow and the S256 challenge method, and a refusal for a public client, service accounts, password grants, the implicit flow, full scope, a wildcard redirect, a wildcard web origin, plain PKCE and an unknown attribute.

title: The emitted provider refuses a redirect and a plaintext server URL
when: Reads a client from a server that answers with a redirect to another TLS host, then builds a provider from a plaintext server URL.
then: Expects the read refused with no request to the redirect target, and the plaintext provider refused at construction.

title: Protected values from the emitted provider print as redacted text for every verb
when: Formats a secret, a client pointer and a migration plan with seven Go formatting verbs.
then: Expects the fixed redacted text for every value and every verb.

title: The emitted provider creates a disabled client, confirms it by saved ID and keeps a conflict
when: Creates a service-account client for two ownership shapes, answers the creation with a foreign Location header, then repeats the creation so the provider answers with a conflict.
then: Expects the nine unsafe flags false, no secret in the request, confirmation through a read of the saved ID, no request to the foreign location, ErrConflict for the repeat, and no replayed creation.

title: The emitted probes follow dependency state without letting probe traffic reach the dependency
when: Runs a monitor whose one check first fails with a private error text, sends 1,600 concurrent readiness requests, then makes the check pass and fail again.
then: Expects 503 before the first sample, 503 with the fixed unavailable body and no-store header while the check fails, exactly one check call for all probe traffic, 200 liveness during the failure, and readiness that follows recovery and the later failure.

title: The emitted monitor bounds each cycle and clears readiness on cancellation
when: Runs a monitor whose check waits for its context, then calls Run again, then cancels the parent context of a second monitor that is ready.
then: Expects the check context closed inside one second, 503 for the late success, a refusal for the second Run call, and 503 right after the parent cancellation.

title: A stalled check in the emitted monitor cannot keep old readiness or start more work
when: Runs a monitor that becomes ready, then holds its second check callback open.
then: Expects readiness to fall to 503 as the last successful cycle expires, exactly two check calls, and 200 liveness during the stall.

title: The assembled service keeps the probe routes public and every other route protected
when: Builds and starts the generated service, then requests the two probe routes and one application route without and with an authorized header.
then: Expects 200 for each probe route, 401 for the unauthenticated application route, 204 for the authorized application route, and a clean shutdown on SIGTERM.

title: The emitted runtime exports no private request data and does not change the response
when: Sends one request that holds a private path, query, body, Authorization header, baggage and trace state through the emitted handler, with dead HTTP proxy variables set, and reads the exported trace.
then: Expects the application status and body unchanged, a valid span context in the handler, one span with two attributes and no trace state, and no private value in the serialized export.

title: The emitted runtime refuses an unsafe collector endpoint and an undeclared setting
when: Builds the runtime with no collector, then with a plaintext, credentialed, path-bearing and query-bearing endpoint, then with five invalid sampling ratios, then with an undeclared resource attribute setting.
then: Expects no provider without a collector, and a refusal for every invalid endpoint, every invalid ratio and the undeclared setting.

title: The emitted runtime does not export to an untrusted collector
when: Removes the collector certificate setting, then observes one request and waits for an export failure.
then: Expects the export failure count to rise and the collector to receive no trace.

title: A blocked collector does not delay the emitted runtime's requests or shutdown
when: Observes three times the queue size in requests against a collector that never answers, then closes the runtime.
then: Expects every request to keep its status, the whole request set to finish inside one second, an export failure to be recorded, and shutdown to finish inside its limit.

title: The emitted runtime authenticates every signal and follows token rotation
when: Exports traces, logs and metrics to a TLS collector that requires one bearer token, replaces the token file, exports again, then makes the token file world readable.
then: Expects every signal accepted with the first token, every signal accepted with the replacement token without a restart, and a refused export after the file permission change.

title: The emitted runtime identity is an opaque UUID and fails closed without entropy
when: Builds an instance ID from a fixed 17-byte reader, then from a short reader and from a reader that returns an error.
then: Expects the canonical UUID v4 encoding from exactly 16 bytes, and an empty value with fixed error text that holds no private detail for each failing reader.

title: The emitted problem type, its constructors and its serializer match RFC 9457
when: Generates a basic service and reads the emitted errors file.
then: Expects the ServiceError members, the seven constructors, the per-category codes, the validation array and the problem content type.

title: The emitted problem serializer reads the trace identifier from the request header
when: Reads the emitted handleError function.
then: Expects it to take the trace identifier from the Traceparent header, and to set the instance and the UTC timestamp.

title: The emitted problem type URI follows the declared error base
when: Generates with a declared error type base, then without one.
then: Expects the base joined to the category slug in the first case and about:blank in the second.

title: The emitted create handler presents the envelope and a time-ordered identifier
when: Generates in envelope mode and reads the emitted create handler.
then: Expects a UUID version 7 identifier, a 500 answer when that call fails, and a presentEntity call that adds id, kind and href.

title: The emitted list handler answers with the paging envelope
when: Generates in envelope mode and reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects the kind, page, size, total and items members of the list envelope.

title: The emitted list handler clamps the page size
when: Reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects the page size to be compared with 65500 and clamped to that value.

title: The emitted list handler refuses an order field that is not an entity field
when: Reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects a valid-field map, a 400 answer for an unknown field and a 400 answer for a direction other than asc or desc.

title: The emitted list handler sorts newest first without an order request
when: Reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects created_time descending as the order when the request supplies no orderBy.

title: The emitted list handler checks the field selection and keeps the identifier
when: Reads the emitted list handler.
then: Expects a 400 answer for an unknown field name and id added to the selection when the request omits it.

title: The emitted upsert handler separates an insert from an update and refuses a stale generation
when: Generates a collection that declares optimistic concurrency and reads the emitted upsert handler.
then: Expects 201 for an insert, 200 for an update, the declared concurrency mode passed to the store, and a 409 conflict problem for the store's conflict error.

title: The emitted patch handler takes only the patchable fields, as pointers
when: Generates a collection with a patchable field list and reads the emitted patch handler.
then: Expects a request type whose members are pointers to the patchable fields only, and a merge that assigns a member only when the request supplies it.

title: The emitted create handler discards client values for server-managed fields
when: Generates an entity with computed, timestamp, created_by, updated_by and generation fields.
then: Expects the handler to clear each of them and then to set them from the verified identity, the current time and the declared default.

title: The emitted update handler keeps create-only values and raises the generation
when: Generates an entity with create-only server-managed fields and a generation field.
then: Expects created_by, created_time and computed fields restored from the stored record, and the generation raised from the stored value instead of from zero.

title: The emitted handlers refuse a body whose kind is not the entity
when: Reads the emitted create handler.
then: Expects a 400 answer when the body carries a kind member that differs from the entity name, and no check when the member is absent.

title: The emitted create-request schema leaves out the fields a client cannot set
when: Generates the OpenAPI document for an entity with server-managed fields.
then: Expects the create-request schema to hold only the client fields, and the POST body to point at that schema.

title: The emitted middleware checks each write body against the embedded document
when: Generates with request validation set to openapi-schema.
then: Expects a middleware that embeds the document, checks POST, PUT and PATCH bodies, and answers a 400 validation problem with per-field details.

title: The emitted middleware gives the request body back to the handler
when: Reads the emitted validation middleware.
then: Expects the body buffered for the check and restored for the handler.

title: The emitted handlers force the collection's implicit field values
when: Generates a collection that declares implicit fields.
then: Expects the create handler to overwrite those fields with their declared constants before it stores the record.

title: The emitted handlers check a scoped record against its parent
when: Generates a scoped collection and reads the emitted read handler.
then: Expects the stored record's scope field compared with the parent path value before the answer.

title: The emitted discovery routes sit outside the authenticated group
when: Generates with a base path and reads the wiring.
then: Expects the OpenAPI, OpenAPI HTML and metadata routes registered on the public multiplexer and not in the protected route list.

title: The emitted HTTPS client keeps one verified origin and all its bounds
when: Runs the emitted client against a TLS test server for a wrong server name, escaping paths, a redirect, an over-large request and response, a deadline, a failed mutation, a closed client and a foreign origin, then its capacity, its credential files, its streams and its certificate pin.
then: Expects each unsafe case refused without reaching the service, the capacity limit refused instead of queued, only private credential modes accepted, every stream bound, and the pin checked beside the CA chain and the server name.

title: The emitted client returns no data when the caller cancels during the response read
when: Cancels the caller's context from inside the response body read.
then: Expects an error with no status and no body, a closed response body and a released request permit.

title: The emitted endpoint verifies, decodes strictly, bounds its work and keeps errors private
when: Sends valid, malformed, aliased, duplicated, over-long and unauthenticated bodies, then empty-status endpoints, dynamic replies, required members, a cancelled body read and a preparation callback.
then: Expects no domain call for a refused request, no-store on every answer, no private error text, empty answers without a body or content type, and the preparation callback run once between decoding and the domain call.

title: The emitted projector keeps the envelope, checks its selectors and bounds every value
when: Projects a list with exact large integers, nested objects, object arrays, nulls and absent members, then invalid selectors, malformed responses, schema bounds, a schema changed after construction, concurrent calls and an absent selection.
then: Expects the envelope, the order and the exact values kept, undeclared data never exposed, each invalid case refused with the right contract error, and the normal path kept when the caller selects nothing.

title: The emitted runtime supervises a managed application and closes it once
when: Runs a handler that supplies Run and Close, cancels it, then closes it twice, then runs a plain handler.
then: Expects one run and one close for the managed handler and no cleanup for the plain handler.

title: The emitted gRPC runtime keeps its transport, identity, admission, isolation and shutdown rules
when: Runs the generated service over real TLS with valid, invalid, duplicated and absent bearer values, over-large messages, concurrent unary calls, server streams at the process and per-identity limits, a blocked stream, a handler panic, a request with no authority, a prepared registrar and shutdown.
then: Expects verified TLS 1.3 only, every method authenticated, each limit held, a fixed internal error for a panic or unknown failure, cleanup in reverse order, and the no-authority request refused with status 400 and the internal gRPC status.

title: The emitted gRPC client requires trusted TLS, a private token and its fixed limits
when: Calls the generated client against a TLS service with a trusted and an untrusted root, a wrong server name, an over-large response, a denied call and a blocked call.
then: Expects only the trusted and correctly named server accepted, the token supplied for each call, and each limit and deadline held.

title: A terminal stream result completes the client observation before it returns
when: Returns a deadline, an error and an end of file from Header and from RecvMsg on a wrapped stream whose transport runs no completion callback.
then: Expects exactly one completion call with the right status code before the wrapper returns, and the terminal result unchanged.

title: The emitted client traces whole calls and whole streams
when: Runs traced unary calls and server streams against a collector, including a held stream.
then: Expects one client span per call with the contract method name, and the complete stream lifetime recorded.
